topics.name: Inorganic Chemistry
concepts: Isotopes of hydrogen: protium (0 n), deuterium (1 n), tritium (2 n, radioactive); D₂O boils at 101.4 °C
Oxides: Na₂O basic, SO₂/SO₃/CO₂ acidic, Al₂O₃/ZnO amphoteric, CO/N₂O/NO neutral [repeat]
Ozone is bent (≈117°); tails mercury; liberates I₂ from KI; destroyed by Cl· from CFCs
Excess NH₃ + Cl₂ → N₂ + NH₄Cl; excess Cl₂ → NCl₃ + HCl
PH₃: white P + conc. NaOH; rotten-fish smell; P₂H₄ impurity makes it catch fire [repeat]
Conc. HNO₃ makes Fe, Al, Cr passive; Cu + conc. HNO₃ → NO₂, Cu + dil. HNO₃ → NO
Cl₂ bleaches by oxidation (permanent); SO₂ by reduction (temporary)
Cl₂ + cold dil. NaOH → NaCl + NaOCl; hot conc. NaOH → NaCl + NaClO₃
Conc. H₂SO₄ chars sugar (dehydrating) and oxidises Cu to CuSO₄ + SO₂ [repeat]
Calcination: carbonates, little/no air; roasting: sulphides, excess air; basic flux CaO removes SiO₂ as CaSiO₃ slag
Copper: Cu₂S + 2Cu₂O → 6Cu + SO₂ (blister Cu); poling then electro-refining; anode mud has Ag, Au
Ores: haematite Fe₂O₃, zinc blende ZnS, cinnabar HgS, argentite Ag₂S; blast-furnace product = pig iron [repeat]
CFT octahedral: t₂g (3, lower) and e_g (2, upper); CFSE = −0.4Δo per t₂g e⁻; CN⁻ strong-field
[Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ square planar (dsp²); [NiCl₄]²⁻ tetrahedral (sp³); calomel Hg₂Cl₂ blackens with NH₃ [repeat]
Co in vitamin B₁₂, Mg in chlorophyll, Fe²⁺ in haemoglobin, Zn in carbonic anhydrase, Ni in urease
Na⁺/K⁺ pump: 3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in per ATP; Minamata = Hg, itai-itai = Cd, plumbism = Pb

topics.name: Organic Chemistry
concepts: Carbon shows maximum catenation (strong C–C bond); hybridisation sp³/sp²/sp for single/double/triple bonds [repeat]
Stability: carbocation & radical 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃; carbanion CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3°
Markovnikov: H to the carbon with more H; peroxide reverses it for HBr only
Lindlar catalyst (Pd/BaSO₄ + quinoline) gives cis-alkene; Na/liq. NH₃ gives trans [repeat]
Octane number: iso-octane 100, n-heptane 0; cetane number is for diesel
Aromatic = planar cyclic conjugated with (4n+2) π electrons; benzene C–C 139 pm
SN2: one step, inversion, CH₃X fastest; SN1: carbocation, racemisation, 3° fastest
Lucas test: 3° alcohol turbid at once, 2° in ~5 min, 1° no turbidity at room temperature
Phenol acidity rises with −NO₂ (p-nitrophenol most acidic), falls with −CH₃ [repeat]
Williamson: RONa + R′X; for tert-butyl ethers use tert-butoxide + CH₃X
Tollens' (silver mirror) given by aldehydes and HCOOH, not ketones; Perkin reaction gives cinnamic acid [repeat]
Acyl reactivity: acid chloride > anhydride > ester > amide; HCOOH (pKa 3.75) stronger than CH₃COOH (4.76) [repeat]
Nitrobenzene (oil of mirbane): Sn/HCl → aniline; Zn/NH₄Cl → N-phenylhydroxylamine [repeat]
Basicity in water: (CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > (CH₃)₃N > NH₃ > aniline
Hoffmann separation with diethyl oxalate: 1° → solid oxamide, 2° → liquid oxamic ester, 3° no reaction
RMgX + HCHO → 1°, + RCHO → 2°, + ketone or ester → 3° alcohol; + RCN → ketone; + CO₂ → acid [repeat]

topics.name: Applied Chemistry
concepts: Haber: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, Fe catalyst + Mo promoter, ~200 atm, 450–500 °C
Contact process uses V₂O₅; Ostwald process oxidises NH₃ on Pt–Rh gauze
Solvay: NaCl + NH₃ + CO₂ → NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃; fails for K₂CO₃ (KHCO₃ too soluble)
Urea: 2NH₃ + CO₂ → ammonium carbamate → urea + H₂O; urea is 46.7% N
Diaphragm cell (brine): Cl₂ at anode, H₂ and NaOH at cathode
Cement: limestone + clay; 2–3% gypsum slows setting
Plaster of Paris CaSO₄·½H₂O; gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O; Epsom salt MgSO₄·7H₂O; bleaching powder Ca(OCl)Cl
Hypo Na₂S₂O₃·5H₂O fixes photographs (dissolves AgBr); lunar caustic = AgNO₃
Formalin = 40% HCHO (preserves specimens); chloropicrin CCl₃NO₂ (tear gas); chloretone (hypnotic)
Teflon = poly(tetrafluoroethene); nylon-6,6 from hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid [repeat]
Indigo is a vat dye; azo dyes contain –N=N– [repeat]
Paracetamol: analgesic and antipyretic; aspirin = acetylsalicylic acid [repeat]
Co-60 for cancer radiotherapy, I-131 for thyroid; blood buffered by H₂CO₃/HCO₃⁻ at pH 7.4

questions.q: Heavy water (D₂O) is used
o: as a moderator in nuclear reactors
questions.x: D₂O slows down fast neutrons, so it is used as a moderator.

questions.q: Temporary hardness of water is due to
questions.x: Bicarbonates of Ca and Mg decompose on boiling to insoluble carbonates, so the hardness is temporary.
questions.trap: CaCl₂/MgSO₄: these cause permanent hardness.

questions.q: The strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution among alkali metals is
questions.x: Li has the most negative E° (−3.04 V) because its very high hydration enthalpy outweighs its high IE.
questions.trap: Cs: it has the lowest IE, but hydration favours Li in water.

questions.q: Plaster of Paris is
questions.x: Heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) at about 393 K gives the hemihydrate CaSO₄·½H₂O.
questions.trap: CaSO₄·2H₂O: that is gypsum, the starting material.
questions.s: Applications of Non-metals, Metals and Compounds – plaster of Paris

questions.q: The Solvay process cannot be used to prepare K₂CO₃ because
o: KHCO₃ is too soluble to be precipitated
questions.x: The process relies on precipitating the bicarbonate; NaHCO₃ precipitates but KHCO₃ is too soluble.
questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – sodium carbonate (Solvay process)

questions.q: The brown ring in the nitrate test is due to
questions.x: NO from nitrate binds to Fe²⁺ to form the brown complex [Fe(H₂O)₅NO]²⁺ at the junction.
questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – nitric acid (nitrate test)

questions.q: In Ostwald's process, ammonia is oxidised to NO using the catalyst
questions.x: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O over Pt–Rh gauze.
questions.trap: Fe: that is the Haber process catalyst.
questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – nitric acid (Ostwald's process)

questions.q: Catalyst used in the contact process for H₂SO₄ is
questions.x: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ is catalysed by V₂O₅.
questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – sulphuric acid (Contact process)

questions.q: The strongest acid in aqueous solution is
questions.x: H–I is the weakest bond, so HI ionises most easily.
questions.trap: HF: F is most electronegative, but its H–F bond is strongest.
questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – HCl, HBr and HI

questions.q: The first noble gas compound, prepared by Bartlett, was
questions.x: Bartlett (1962) noted O₂ and Xe have similar IE; O₂⁺[PtF₆]⁻ existed, so he made Xe⁺[PtF₆]⁻.
questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – noble gases (not in 2026 syllabus)

questions.q: Which ion is colourless in aqueous solution?
questions.x: Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰, so no d–d transition is possible.

questions.q: Spin-only magnetic moment of Fe³⁺ (Z of Fe = 26) is about
questions.trap: 4.90 BM: that is Fe²⁺ (n = 4).

questions.q: Oxidation state of Mn in KMnO₄ is
Froth flotation is used to concentrate
questions.x: Sulphide ore particles are wetted by pine oil and rise with the froth; gangue is wetted by water.
questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – concentration of ores

questions.q: Coordination number of Co in [Co(en)₃]³⁺ is
questions.x: en (ethylenediamine) is bidentate; 3 × 2 = 6 donor atoms.
questions.trap: 3: counting ligands instead of donor atoms.
questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – shape of complex ions

questions.q: Oxidation state of Fe in K₄[Fe(CN)₆] is
questions.trap: +3: confusing with K₃[Fe(CN)₆].

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH(OH)–CH₃ is
questions.x: Longest chain has 4 C; number from the end nearer –OH: OH on C2, methyl on C3.
questions.trap: 2-methylbutan-3-ol: giving the substituent, not –OH, the lower number.

questions.q: Number of structurally isomeric alcohols of formula C₄H₁₀O is
questions.x: Butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol = 4.
questions.trap: 7: also counting the three ethers.

questions.q: Which compound is optically active?
questions.x: C2 of butan-2-ol carries H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅: four different groups, so it is chiral.

questions.q: The most stable carbocation is
questions.x: Tertiary carbocation is most stabilised by +I effect and hyperconjugation of nine C–H bonds.

questions.q: The strongest acid among the following is
questions.x: F has the strongest −I effect, best stabilising the carboxylate anion.
questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties

questions.q: Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of peroxide to give mainly
questions.x: Peroxide causes anti-Markovnikov (Kharasch) free-radical addition, Br going to the terminal carbon.
questions.trap: 2-bromopropane: the Markovnikov product without peroxide.

questions.q: Ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene, (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃, gives
questions.x: Cleaving C=C: (CH₃)₂C= gives (CH₃)₂C=O (propanone); =CHCH₃ gives CH₃CHO (ethanal).

questions.q: Which gives a white precipitate with ammoniacal AgNO₃?
questions.x: Only terminal alkynes have acidic ≡C–H; propyne forms silver propynide.
questions.trap: But-2-yne: it is an alkyne but has no terminal H.

questions.q: The electrophile in nitration of benzene is
questions.x: Conc. H₂SO₄ protonates HNO₃ to generate the nitronium ion NO₂⁺.
questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene

questions.q: Ethyl bromide heated with sodium in dry ether gives
questions.x: Wurtz reaction: 2C₂H₅Br + 2Na → C₄H₁₀ + 2NaBr.

questions.q: Phenol with CHCl₃ and aqueous NaOH gives mainly
questions.x: Reimer–Tiemann reaction introduces –CHO at the ortho position of phenol.
questions.trap: Salicylic acid: that forms with CCl₄ or in Kolbe's reaction.
questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol

questions.q: Clemmensen reduction of a ketone uses
questions.x: Zinc amalgam with conc. HCl reduces C=O to CH₂.
questions.trap: NH₂NH₂/KOH: that is Wolff–Kishner reduction.

questions.q: Which undergoes SN1 reaction fastest?
questions.x: SN1 goes through a carbocation; tertiary carbocation is most stable.
questions.trap: CH₃Br: that is fastest for SN2, not SN1.

questions.q: The most acidic compound is
questions.x: –NO₂ withdraws electrons and stabilises the phenoxide ion; –CH₃ in p-cresol does the opposite.
questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol

questions.q: Which gives a positive iodoform test?
questions.x: Ethanol is oxidised to CH₃CHO, which has the CH₃CO– group needed for iodoform.
questions.trap: Methanol: it lacks the CH₃–CH(OH)– unit.

questions.q: Cannizzaro reaction is given by
questions.x: Cannizzaro needs an aldehyde with no α-hydrogen; C₆H₅CHO has none.
questions.trap: Acetaldehyde: it has α-H and undergoes aldol instead.

questions.q: Propanamide on treatment with Br₂ and KOH gives
questions.x: Hofmann bromamide: RCONH₂ → RNH₂ with one carbon less; C₂H₅CONH₂ → C₂H₅NH₂.
questions.trap: Propan-1-amine: forgetting the loss of one carbon.

questions.q: Carbylamine test is given by
questions.x: Only primary amines with CHCl₃ and alcoholic KOH form foul-smelling isocyanides.

questions.q: The weakest base among the following is
questions.x: In aniline the N lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring, so it is less available.

questions.q: Nylon-6,6 is made from
questions.x: Condensation of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid (each 6 C) gives nylon-6,6.
questions.trap: Caprolactam: that gives nylon-6.
questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – polymer

questions.q: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives
questions.x: Sucrose is a disaccharide of α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose.
questions.trap: Glucose + galactose: that is lactose.
questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – (carbohydrates; not in 2026 syllabus)

questions.q: Aspirin is chemically
questions.x: Aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid, an analgesic and antipyretic.
questions.trap: p-Acetamidophenol: that is paracetamol.
questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – drugs

questions.q: Nascent hydrogen is a stronger reducing agent than ordinary H₂ because it
o: exists momentarily as reactive atomic hydrogen
questions.x: Hydrogen at the moment of generation is atomic; no H–H bond (436 kJ/mol) has to be broken, so it reduces readily.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – isotopes of hydrogen
questions.q: Number of neutrons in a tritium nucleus is
questions.x: Tritium ³H has 1 proton and 3 − 1 = 2 neutrons.
questions.trap: 1: that is deuterium.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – isotopes of hydrogen
questions.q: The radioactive isotope of hydrogen is
questions.x: Tritium (³H) is a β-emitter, half-life about 12.3 years; protium and deuterium are stable.

questions.q: Compared with ordinary water, heavy water (D₂O) has
questions.x: D₂O: bp 101.4 °C, fp 3.8 °C, density about 1.1 g/cm³, all higher than H₂O.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – types of oxides
questions.q: Which oxide is amphoteric?
questions.x: Al₂O₃ reacts with both acids and bases (forming Al³⁺ salts and aluminates).
questions.trap: CO: it is neutral, not amphoteric.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – types of oxides
questions.q: Which of these is a neutral oxide?
questions.x: CO, N₂O and NO are neutral oxides; CO₂ and SO₂ are acidic, Na₂O basic.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – types of oxides
questions.q: SO₂ dissolves in water to give a solution that is
questions.x: SO₂ is an acidic oxide: SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃ (sulphurous acid), which turns blue litmus red.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – structure of ozone
questions.q: Shape of the ozone (O₃) molecule is
questions.x: Central O has one lone pair and is sp²; O₃ is angular with bond angle ≈ 116.8° and equal O–O bonds (resonance).
questions.trap: Ring: O₃ is not cyclic.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – test of ozone
questions.q: Ozone makes mercury lose its meniscus and stick to glass. This is called
questions.x: O₃ oxidises Hg to Hg₂O, which dissolves in Hg and makes it stick to glass: a standard test for ozone.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – ozone layer depletion
questions.q: Ozone layer depletion in the stratosphere is mainly caused by
questions.x: UV splits CFCs to give Cl·; Cl· + O₃ → ClO· + O₂, and ClO· regenerates Cl·, so one Cl destroys many O₃.
questions.trap: CO₂: a greenhouse gas, not an ozone destroyer.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – chemical properties of ammonia
questions.q: When excess ammonia reacts with chlorine, the products are
questions.x: 8NH₃ + 3Cl₂ → N₂ + 6NH₄Cl. With excess Cl₂ instead: NH₃ + 3Cl₂ → NCl₃ + 3HCl.
questions.trap: NCl₃ + HCl: that is with excess chlorine.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – chemical properties of ammonia
questions.q: Excess ammonia added to CuSO₄ solution gives a deep blue colour due to
questions.x: First pale blue Cu(OH)₂ precipitates; excess NH₃ dissolves it as deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) ion.
questions.trap: Cu(OH)₂: the pale blue precipitate before excess NH₃.

questions.q: Phosphine is prepared in the laboratory by heating white phosphorus with
questions.x: P₄ + 3NaOH + 3H₂O → PH₃ + 3NaH₂PO₂ (in an inert atmosphere).

questions.q: Phosphine (PH₃) has a smell like
questions.x: PH₃ smells of rotten fish; H₂S smells of rotten eggs; nitrobenzene/HCN of bitter almonds.
questions.trap: Rotten eggs: that is H₂S.

questions.q: Phosphine prepared from white phosphorus catches fire in air because it contains
questions.x: Pure PH₃ is not spontaneously inflammable; the P₂H₄ (diphosphane) impurity ignites, giving vortex rings of P₄O₁₀.

questions.q: White phosphorus glows faintly in the dark because of
questions.x: The glow (traditionally called phosphorescence) is chemiluminescence from slow oxidation of P₄ vapour in air.

questions.q: Iron is rendered passive by
questions.x: Conc. HNO₃ forms a thin protective oxide film on Fe (also Al, Cr), stopping further reaction.

questions.q: Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid to give mainly
questions.x: Cu + 4HNO₃(conc) → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O; dilute acid gives NO.
questions.trap: NO: from dilute HNO₃.

questions.q: In the laboratory, chlorine is prepared by heating conc. HCl with
questions.x: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O; MnO₂ oxidises HCl.

questions.q: Chlorine reacts with cold, dilute NaOH to give
questions.x: Cl₂ + 2NaOH(cold, dil) → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O (disproportionation).
questions.trap: NaClO₃: that needs hot, concentrated NaOH.

questions.q: With hot concentrated NaOH, chlorine forms NaCl and NaClO₃ in the mole ratio
questions.x: 3Cl₂ + 6NaOH → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O; Cl goes 0 → −1 (5 atoms) and 0 → +5 (1 atom).

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – bleaching by chlorine and SO₂
questions.q: Bleaching by SO₂ is temporary because it acts by
o: reduction, and air later re-oxidises the colour
questions.x: SO₂ (with moisture) gives nascent H which reduces the dye; air re-oxidises it. Cl₂ bleaches by oxidation, which is permanent.
questions.trap: Oxidation: that is chlorine's permanent bleaching.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – HCl, HBr and HI
questions.q: HI cannot be prepared by heating NaI with conc. H₂SO₄ because
o: NaI does not react with acids
questions.x: HI (and HBr) are reducing; conc. H₂SO₄ oxidises them to I₂/Br₂. Non-oxidising H₃PO₄ is used instead.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – HCl, HBr and HI
questions.q: Reducing power of the hydrogen halides decreases in the order
questions.x: Bond strength falls from H–F to H–I, so HI gives up H/electrons most easily and is the strongest reducing agent.

questions.q: Iodine gives a blue-black colour with
questions.x: I₂ enters the starch (amylose) helix to give the blue-black complex: test for iodine.
questions.trap: Chloroform: iodine dissolves to a violet solution, not blue-black.

questions.q: Iodine is much more soluble in aqueous KI than in water because it forms
questions.x: I₂ + I⁻ ⇌ I₃⁻ (triiodide), so KI solution dissolves much more iodine.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – allotropes of carbon
questions.q: Graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not, because in graphite
o: the layers are joined by strong covalent bonds
each carbon is sp² and has one delocalised electron
questions.x: Graphite: sp² layers with one free (delocalised) electron per C that moves along the layers. Diamond: all four electrons in sp³ σ bonds.
questions.trap: sp³: that describes diamond.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – allotropes of carbon
questions.q: Buckminsterfullerene, C₆₀, is made of
questions.x: C₆₀ is a soccer-ball cage: 12 five-membered and 20 six-membered rings; each C is sp².

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – allotropes of carbon
questions.q: Hybridisation of carbon in diamond is
questions.x: Each C in diamond is tetrahedrally bonded to four others (sp³), giving a rigid 3D network.
questions.trap: sp²: that is graphite.

questions.q: Carbon monoxide is poisonous because it
o: binds haemoglobin far more strongly than O₂, forming carboxyhaemoglobin
questions.x: CO forms a stable complex with the Fe²⁺ of haemoglobin, so blood cannot carry O₂.

questions.q: Heating impure nickel in CO at about 330–350 K gives
questions.x: Mond process: Ni + 4CO → Ni(CO)₄; it decomposes at higher temperature to pure Ni.

questions.q: H₂S gas turns lead acetate paper black because of formation of
questions.x: Pb(CH₃COO)₂ + H₂S → PbS (black) + 2CH₃COOH.

questions.q: When H₂S is passed into acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, the solution turns green and a yellow solid separates. H₂S acts as
questions.x: H₂S is oxidised to S (yellow) and reduces Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) to Cr³⁺ (green).

questions.q: SO₂ turns acidified potassium dichromate paper
questions.x: SO₂ reduces Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) to Cr³⁺ (green): test for SO₂.

questions.q: Conc. H₂SO₄ chars sugar because it acts as a
questions.x: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ → 12C + 11H₂O; conc. H₂SO₄ removes the elements of water, leaving black carbon.

questions.q: Hot conc. H₂SO₄ reacts with copper to give
questions.x: Cu + 2H₂SO₄(conc) → CuSO₄ + SO₂ + 2H₂O; acid acts as an oxidising agent.
questions.trap: H₂: copper is below H, so no H₂.

questions.q: The strongest oxidising agent among the halogens is
questions.x: F₂ has the highest E° (+2.87 V) because of low F–F bond energy and high hydration energy of F⁻.

questions.q: Calcination is heating an ore
o: with a flux to form slag
below its melting point in the absence or limited supply of air
in excess air to convert sulphide to oxide
questions.x: Calcination drives out CO₂/H₂O from carbonate and hydrated ores, e.g. ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂.
questions.trap: Excess air: that is roasting.

questions.q: Roasting is mainly used for
questions.x: Sulphide ores are heated in excess air: 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – flux and slag
questions.q: To remove silica (SiO₂) gangue, the flux used is
questions.x: Acidic gangue needs a basic flux: CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ (slag).
questions.trap: SiO₂: an acidic flux, used for basic gangue like FeO.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – flux and slag
questions.q: The slag formed in the blast furnace extraction of iron is
questions.x: Limestone gives CaO, which combines with SiO₂: CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃.
questions.trap: FeSiO₃: slag in copper extraction, not iron.

questions.q: In the thermite (aluminothermic) process, Cr₂O₃ is reduced by
questions.x: Cr₂O₃ + 2Al → 2Cr + Al₂O₃, strongly exothermic because Al has very high affinity for oxygen.

questions.q: Zone refining is used to obtain ultra-pure
questions.x: Impurities are more soluble in the melt, so a moving molten zone sweeps them to one end; used for semiconductors.

questions.q: Poling is used in the purification of
questions.x: Green wooden poles stir molten impure Cu; the hydrocarbons reduce Cu₂O to Cu.

questions.q: In bessemerization of copper matte, metallic copper forms by the reaction
questions.x: In the Bessemer converter FeS is removed as FeSiO₃ slag, then part of Cu₂S oxidises to Cu₂O, which reacts with remaining Cu₂S (self-reduction).

questions.q: Blister copper gets its blistered look because
o: dissolved SO₂ escapes as it solidifies
it contains air bubbles from poling
questions.x: SO₂ produced during self-reduction escapes on cooling, leaving blisters; blister Cu is about 98% pure.

questions.q: Zinc blende is
questions.x: Zinc blende = ZnS; calamine = ZnCO₃; zincite = ZnO.
questions.trap: ZnCO₃: that is calamine.

questions.q: Cinnabar is the chief ore of
questions.x: Cinnabar is HgS; Hg is obtained by roasting: HgS + O₂ → Hg + SO₂.

questions.q: Haematite is
questions.x: Haematite Fe₂O₃; magnetite Fe₃O₄; siderite FeCO₃; iron pyrites FeS₂.
questions.trap: Fe₃O₄: that is magnetite.

questions.q: In the cyanide process for silver, the metal is finally recovered by adding
questions.x: Ag dissolves as Na[Ag(CN)₂]; Zn displaces it: 2[Ag(CN)₂]⁻ + Zn → [Zn(CN)₄]²⁻ + 2Ag.

questions.q: The main reducing agent in the blast furnace for iron is
questions.x: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ in the upper (cooler) zone; CO comes from coke.

questions.q: Iron obtained directly from the blast furnace is called
questions.x: Pig iron contains about 4% carbon plus Si, Mn, P, S; wrought iron is the purest commercial iron.
questions.trap: Wrought iron: purest form, made from cast iron.

questions.q: In the basic oxygen (L–D) process, steel is made by
o: blowing pure oxygen onto molten pig iron
blowing hot air through molten iron
questions.x: Pure O₂ oxidises excess C, Si, Mn and P quickly; the oxides leave as gases or slag with lime.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – corrosion of iron
questions.q: Rust is chiefly
questions.x: Rusting needs both O₂ and water; the product is hydrated iron(III) oxide.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – corrosion of iron
questions.q: Galvanised iron is iron coated with
questions.x: Zn is more reactive than Fe and corrodes first (sacrificial protection) even if the coat is scratched.
questions.trap: Tin: that is tin-plating, which only protects while unbroken.

questions.q: Potassium salts give a flame colour that is
questions.x: Na golden yellow, K lilac, Li crimson, Ba apple green.

questions.q: Sodium metal is stored under kerosene because it
o: is a liquid at room temperature
reacts vigorously with air and moisture
questions.x: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂; Na also oxidises quickly in air.

questions.q: The only alkali metal that combines directly with nitrogen to form a nitride is
questions.x: 6Li + N₂ → 2Li₃N; anomalous behaviour of Li due to its small size (resembles Mg).

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – alkaline earth metals
questions.q: The least soluble sulphate in water is
questions.x: Solubility of group-2 sulphates falls down the group because hydration energy falls faster than lattice energy.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – alkaline earth metals
questions.q: Thermal stability of alkaline earth carbonates
questions.x: Larger cations polarise CO₃²⁻ less, so BaCO₃ needs the highest temperature to decompose.

questions.q: Aluminium dissolves in NaOH solution with evolution of
questions.x: 2Al + 2NaOH + 2H₂O → 2NaAlO₂ + 3H₂.

questions.q: Zinc reacts with hot NaOH solution to form
questions.x: Zn + 2NaOH → Na₂ZnO₂ (sodium zincate) + H₂; Zn is amphoteric.

questions.q: Transition metals show variable oxidation states because
o: (n−1)d and ns electrons have similar energies
questions.x: Both ns and (n−1)d electrons can be lost/shared since the energy gap is small.

questions.q: Most transition metal ions are coloured because of
questions.x: Ligands split the d orbitals; absorption of visible light promotes an electron between them. d⁰ and d¹⁰ ions are colourless.

questions.q: Which ion has a spin-only magnetic moment of about 1.73 BM?
questions.x: μ = √(n(n+2)); n = 1 gives √3 = 1.73. Ti³⁺ is 3d¹. Mn²⁺ and Fe³⁺ (d⁵) give 5.92; Zn²⁺ gives 0.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – shape of complex ions
questions.q: Shape of [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is
questions.x: Strong-field CN⁻ pairs the d⁸ electrons, leaving one 3d orbital for dsp² hybridisation: square planar, diamagnetic.
questions.trap: Tetrahedral: that is [NiCl₄]²⁻ with weak-field Cl⁻.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – shape of complex ions
questions.q: [NiCl₄]²⁻ is
questions.x: Cl⁻ is weak-field; Ni²⁺ (3d⁸) keeps 2 unpaired electrons and uses sp³: tetrahedral, paramagnetic.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – crystal field theory
questions.q: In an octahedral crystal field, the d orbitals split into
o: lower t₂g (3 orbitals) and higher e_g (2 orbitals)
questions.x: Ligands approach along axes, so d(x²−y²) and d(z²) (e_g) are raised; dxy, dyz, dxz (t₂g) are lowered.
questions.trap: Lower e, higher t₂: that is the tetrahedral pattern.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – crystal field theory
questions.q: Crystal field stabilisation energy of a d³ ion in an octahedral field is
questions.x: All 3 electrons go into t₂g: 3 × (−0.4 Δo) = −1.2 Δo.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – crystal field theory
questions.q: Which is a strong-field ligand?
questions.x: Spectrochemical series: I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – crystal field theory
questions.q: [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is diamagnetic because
o: Fe²⁺ (d⁶) is low-spin with all six electrons paired in t₂g
Fe has no d electrons in it
questions.x: Strong-field CN⁻ makes Δo larger than pairing energy, so t₂g⁶ e_g⁰: no unpaired electrons.

questions.q: Blue vitriol heated to about 250 °C gives
questions.x: CuSO₄·5H₂O loses all water of crystallisation; much stronger heating (>700 °C) gives CuO.
questions.trap: CuO: needs far higher temperature.

questions.q: CuSO₄ solution with KI gives a white precipitate and brown solution. The white precipitate is
questions.x: 2CuSO₄ + 4KI → 2CuI↓ + I₂ + 2K₂SO₄; Cu²⁺ oxidises I⁻ to I₂ (brown) and becomes Cu⁺.
questions.trap: CuI₂: unstable, decomposes at once.

questions.q: White vitriol is
questions.x: White vitriol ZnSO₄·7H₂O; blue vitriol CuSO₄·5H₂O; green vitriol FeSO₄·7H₂O; Epsom salt MgSO₄·7H₂O.

questions.q: Calomel turns black with ammonia solution because it forms
questions.x: Hg₂Cl₂ + 2NH₃ → Hg (black) + Hg(NH₂)Cl (white) + NH₄Cl; the mixture looks black.

questions.q: Chemical formula of calomel is
questions.x: Calomel = mercury(I) chloride Hg₂Cl₂; corrosive sublimate = mercury(II) chloride HgCl₂.
questions.trap: HgCl₂: corrosive sublimate.

questions.q: HgCl₂ solution with excess SnCl₂ finally gives
questions.x: 2HgCl₂ + SnCl₂ → Hg₂Cl₂ (white) + SnCl₄; then Hg₂Cl₂ + SnCl₂ → 2Hg (grey) + SnCl₄.
questions.trap: White ppt: that is the first stage (Hg₂Cl₂).

questions.q: The green coating on copper exposed to moist air is
questions.x: Moist air with CO₂ forms green basic copper carbonate (patina).

questions.q: Mercury is stored in iron containers because
o: iron does not form an amalgam with mercury
questions.x: Most metals dissolve in Hg as amalgams; Fe (and Pt) do not.

questions.q: In the electrolytic refining of copper, the anode mud contains
questions.x: Impure Cu is the anode; less reactive metals do not dissolve and fall below the anode. Fe, Zn go into solution.
questions.trap: Fe and Zn: more reactive, they dissolve.

questions.q: Sodium is extracted by
questions.x: Highly electropositive metals cannot be reduced by C; fused NaCl (with CaCl₂) is electrolysed (Downs cell).
questions.trap: Aqueous NaCl: gives H₂ at the cathode, not Na.

questions.s: Bio-inorganic Chemistry – micro and macro nutrients
questions.q: Which is a micronutrient (trace element) in the human body?
questions.x: Na, K, Ca, Mg are macro elements needed in large amounts; Zn, Cu, Co, Cr, Ni are trace elements.

questions.q: Cobalt is a constituent of
questions.x: Vitamin B₁₂ (cobalamin) has Co at its centre; deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

questions.q: The metal at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule is
questions.x: Chlorophyll is a Mg-porphyrin; haem is an Fe-porphyrin.
questions.trap: Fe: that is haem.

questions.q: Oxidation state of iron in functional (oxygen-carrying) haemoglobin is
questions.x: O₂ binds only to Fe²⁺; oxidised Fe³⁺ (methaemoglobin) cannot carry oxygen.

questions.q: For each ATP used, the sodium-potassium pump moves
questions.x: Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumps 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in, keeping inside of cell negative.

questions.q: Zinc is an essential part of the enzyme
questions.x: Carbonic anhydrase (Zn²⁺) catalyses CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃; urease contains Ni.
questions.trap: Urease: contains Ni, not Zn.

questions.q: The metal present in the enzyme urease is
questions.x: Urease (which hydrolyses urea to NH₃ and CO₂) has two Ni²⁺ ions in its active site.

questions.q: Trivalent chromium (Cr³⁺) in the body helps in
questions.x: Cr³⁺ is part of the glucose tolerance factor, which enhances insulin action.

questions.q: Ca²⁺ ions are needed in the body for
questions.x: Ca²⁺ is clotting factor IV, triggers muscle contraction and forms bones and teeth.

questions.q: Glucose is absorbed in the intestine by a symport carrier together with
questions.x: The sodium-glucose co-transporter (SGLT1) uses the Na⁺ gradient made by the Na⁺/K⁺ pump to carry glucose in.

questions.q: Minamata disease is caused by poisoning with
questions.x: Methylmercury from industrial waste accumulated in fish in Minamata Bay, Japan.
questions.trap: Cadmium: causes itai-itai disease.

questions.q: Itai-itai disease (painful brittle bones) is caused by
questions.x: Cd from mining waste in rice paddies (Japan) damaged kidneys and bones.

questions.q: Excess accumulation of iron in body organs causes
questions.x: Iron overload deposits in liver, heart and pancreas. Wilson's disease is copper accumulation.
questions.trap: Anaemia: iron deficiency, the opposite.

questions.q: 'Blackfoot disease' and skin lesions from contaminated groundwater are due to
questions.x: Chronic arsenic in tube-well water (also a problem in the Terai) causes skin lesions, gangrene and cancers.

questions.q: Plumbism (saturnism) refers to poisoning by
questions.x: Latin plumbum = lead; lead affects nerves, kidneys and haem synthesis (anaemia).

questions.q: Carbon shows the maximum catenation among elements mainly because
o: the C–C bond is very strong
questions.x: C–C bond energy (~348 kJ/mol) is high and close to C–H, so long chains and rings are stable. Si–Si is much weaker.

questions.q: Hybridisation of carbon atoms in ethyne (HC≡CH) is
questions.x: Triple-bonded carbon uses two sp orbitals (linear, 180°) and two unhybridised p orbitals for π bonds.

questions.s: General Organic Chemistry – sigma and pi bonds
questions.q: Number of σ and π bonds in CH₂=CH–C≡CH is
questions.x: 4 C–H + 3 C–C σ = 7 σ; C=C has 1 π and C≡C has 2 π = 3 π.

questions.q: Successive members of a homologous series differ by
questions.x: e.g. CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈ … each step adds CH₂ = 12 + 2 = 14 u.

questions.q: Ethanol and dimethyl ether are
questions.x: Both are C₂H₆O but contain different functional groups (–OH vs –O–).

questions.q: Diethyl ether and methyl propyl ether are
questions.x: Same functional group, different alkyl groups on either side of –O–: metamerism.

questions.q: Number of structural isomers of pentane (C₅H₁₂) is
questions.x: n-pentane, 2-methylbutane (isopentane), 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane).

questions.q: Which alkene shows geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
questions.x: Each double-bond carbon must carry two different groups: CH₃CH=CHCH₃ does; the others have =CH₂ or =C(CH₃)₂.

questions.q: Total number of stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutane is
questions.x: Two chiral carbons with identical halves: a pair of enantiomers plus one optically inactive meso form = 3.
questions.trap: 4: forgetting the meso form (2ⁿ rule fails here).

questions.q: Homolytic fission of a covalent bond produces
questions.x: Each atom keeps one electron of the shared pair; heterolytic fission gives ions.

questions.s: General Organic Chemistry – electrophile and nucleophile
questions.q: Which is an electrophile?
questions.x: BF₃ has an incomplete octet on B and accepts an electron pair; NH₃, H₂O and CN⁻ donate pairs (nucleophiles).

questions.q: The most stable carbanion is
questions.x: Alkyl groups (+I) push electrons onto the already negative carbon, destabilising it: CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3°.
questions.trap: (CH₃)₃C⁻: reversing the carbocation order.

questions.q: Hybridisation of the positively charged carbon in a carbocation is
questions.x: The carbocation carbon has three σ bonds and an empty p orbital: trigonal planar sp².

questions.q: Which group has the strongest −I effect?
questions.x: −I order: –NO₂ > –CN > –COOH > –F > –Cl > –Br > –I > –OH > –C₆H₅.

questions.q: Which alkyl group has the greatest +I effect?
questions.x: +I increases with branching: tert-butyl > isopropyl > ethyl > methyl.

questions.q: All six C–C bonds in benzene are equal (139 pm) because of
questions.x: π electrons are spread over all six carbons, so each bond lies between C–C (154 pm) and C=C (134 pm).

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ is
questions.x: Longest chain = 5 C; methyl on C-3 from either end.
questions.trap: 2-ethylbutane: longest chain not chosen.

questions.q: IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃C–CH₂CH₃ is
questions.x: Longest chain 4 C; two methyls on C-2 (lowest locants).
questions.trap: 3,3-: numbering from the wrong end.

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₂=CH–CH₂–OH is
questions.x: –OH (principal group) gets the lowest locant (C-1); the double bond is then between C-2 and C-3.

questions.q: The octane number of iso-octane (2,2,4-trimethylpentane) is taken as
questions.x: Reference scale: iso-octane = 100, n-heptane = 0; higher octane number = less knocking.

questions.q: Cetane number is used to rate the quality of
questions.x: Cetane (n-hexadecane) = 100 and α-methylnaphthalene = 0; measures ease of ignition in diesel engines.
questions.trap: Petrol: rated by octane number.

questions.q: Tetraethyl lead (TEL), formerly added to petrol, acts as
questions.x: TEL raises octane number; it is now banned (lead pollution) and replaced by MTBE etc.

questions.q: Breaking higher alkanes into smaller alkanes and alkenes by heating in the absence of air is
questions.x: e.g. C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄; used to get more petrol from heavy fractions.

questions.q: Catalytic reforming of petrol
o: converts straight-chain alkanes to branched and aromatic ones, raising octane number
breaks large molecules into small ones
questions.x: Reforming (Pt catalyst) changes molecular shape (isomerisation, cyclisation, aromatisation) for better antiknock quality.
questions.trap: Breaking molecules: that is cracking.

questions.q: Electrolysis of aqueous sodium acetate (Kolbe's method) gives at the anode
questions.x: 2CH₃COO⁻ → C₂H₆ + 2CO₂ + 2e⁻; two methyl radicals join.

questions.q: Sodium propanoate heated with soda lime gives
questions.x: Decarboxylation removes one C: C₂H₅COONa + NaOH → C₂H₆ + Na₂CO₃.
questions.trap: Propane: forgetting a carbon is lost as CO₂.

questions.q: A mixture of CH₃Br and C₂H₅Br treated with Na in dry ether gives
questions.x: Wurtz coupling of two different halides gives all combinations: CH₃–CH₃, CH₃–C₂H₅, C₂H₅–C₂H₅.

questions.q: Ethane reacts with Cl₂ in diffused sunlight by
questions.x: Light splits Cl₂ into Cl· radicals; chain reaction gives C₂H₅Cl + HCl.

questions.q: Ethanol heated with excess conc. H₂SO₄ at about 443 K (170 °C) gives
questions.x: Intramolecular dehydration: C₂H₅OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. At 413 K with excess alcohol, ether forms.
questions.trap: Diethyl ether: lower temperature (413 K), excess alcohol.

questions.q: 2-Bromobutane heated with alcoholic KOH gives mainly
questions.x: Saytzeff rule: the more substituted alkene is the major product of dehydrohalogenation.
questions.trap: Butan-2-ol: aqueous KOH gives substitution.

questions.q: Propene reacts with HBr (no peroxide) to give mainly
questions.x: Markovnikov: H adds to CH₂ end, giving the more stable 2° carbocation and then 2-bromopropane.

questions.q: Ethene with cold, dilute alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent) gives
questions.x: Syn-addition of two –OH groups; pink colour disappears (test for unsaturation).

questions.q: Ethene decolourises bromine water forming
questions.x: CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → BrCH₂–CH₂Br; red-brown colour disappears.

questions.q: Ethyne passed into dilute H₂SO₄ containing HgSO₄ gives
questions.x: Hydration gives vinyl alcohol, which tautomerises to CH₃CHO.

questions.q: Hydration of propyne (HgSO₄/dil. H₂SO₄) gives
questions.x: Markovnikov addition puts –OH on C-2; the enol tautomerises to CH₃COCH₃.
questions.trap: Propanal: only ethyne gives an aldehyde.

questions.q: Ethyne is prepared in the laboratory from
questions.x: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → C₂H₂ + Ca(OH)₂.

questions.q: Ethyne passed through a red-hot iron tube gives
questions.x: Cyclic trimerisation: 3C₂H₂ → C₆H₆.

questions.q: Partial hydrogenation of but-2-yne with Lindlar catalyst gives
questions.x: Lindlar (Pd/BaSO₄ poisoned with quinoline) adds H₂ syn and stops at the alkene: cis. Na in liquid NH₃ gives trans.
questions.trap: trans: that is Birch-type Na/liq. NH₃.

questions.q: The function of Lindlar catalyst is to
o: oxidise an alkene to a diol
reduce an alkene to an alkane
convert an alkyne to an aldehyde
reduce an alkyne only up to an alkene
questions.x: The poisoned Pd catalyst is too weak to hydrogenate the alkene further.

questions.q: Ethyne is more acidic than ethene and ethane because its carbon is
questions.x: More s-character holds the C–H electron pair closer, stabilising the acetylide anion.

questions.q: Which gives a red precipitate with ammoniacal Cu₂Cl₂?
questions.x: Terminal alkynes (≡C–H) form copper acetylide (red); internal alkynes cannot.

questions.q: Which species is aromatic?
questions.x: Planar, cyclic, conjugated with 6 π electrons (4n+2, n = 1). The cation has 4 π (antiaromatic); COT is non-planar.

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: Benzene with CH₃Cl and anhydrous AlCl₃ gives
questions.x: Friedel–Crafts alkylation: AlCl₃ generates CH₃⁺ electrophile.

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: The electrophile in sulphonation of benzene with fuming H₂SO₄ is
questions.x: SO₃ (electron-poor S) attacks the ring to give benzenesulphonic acid.

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: Benzene with chlorine in bright sunlight (no catalyst) gives
questions.x: UV light causes free-radical addition of 3Cl₂: BHC (gammexane isomer is an insecticide).
questions.trap: Chlorobenzene: that needs FeCl₃ in the dark (substitution).

questions.q: Phenol is converted to benzene by distilling with
questions.x: C₆H₅OH + Zn → C₆H₆ + ZnO.

questions.q: Sodium benzoate heated with soda lime gives
questions.x: Decarboxylation: C₆H₅COONa + NaOH → C₆H₆ + Na₂CO₃.

questions.q: Number of σ bonds in a benzene molecule is
questions.x: 6 C–C σ + 6 C–H σ = 12 σ; plus 3 π (delocalised).

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: Which group is meta-directing in electrophilic substitution of benzene?
questions.x: Electron-withdrawing –NO₂, –CHO, –COOH, –CN direct meta; –OH, –NH₂, –CH₃ and halogens direct ortho/para.
questions.trap: –Cl: deactivating but still ortho/para.

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: Ozonolysis of benzene followed by Zn/H₂O gives
questions.x: Benzene (Kekulé form) adds 3 O₃ to give a triozonide; each C=C splits, giving 3 OHC–CHO.

questions.q: Which reacts fastest by the SN2 mechanism?
questions.x: SN2 needs backside attack; least steric hindrance at CH₃X makes it fastest: CH₃ > 1° > 2° > 3°.
questions.trap: (CH₃)₃CBr: fastest for SN1, slowest for SN2.

questions.q: An SN2 reaction at a chiral carbon gives
questions.x: Nucleophile enters opposite to the leaving group (Walden inversion), single step.

questions.q: An SN1 reaction of an optically active halide gives mainly
questions.x: The planar carbocation intermediate can be attacked from both faces equally.

questions.s: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes – properties of monohaloalkanes
questions.q: For the same alkyl group, reactivity of haloalkanes in substitution is
questions.x: C–I is the weakest bond and I⁻ the best leaving group.

questions.q: (CH₃)₃C–Cl is a
questions.x: The C bearing Cl is attached to three other carbons.

questions.s: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes – properties of monohaloalkanes
questions.q: Ethyl bromide with alcoholic AgCN gives mainly
questions.x: AgCN is covalent; attack occurs through N, giving C₂H₅NC. KCN (ionic) gives C₂H₅CN.
questions.trap: Ethyl cyanide: that is with KCN.

questions.s: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes – properties of monohaloalkanes
questions.q: Bromoethane boiled with aqueous KOH gives
questions.x: Aqueous OH⁻ substitutes Br: C₂H₅Br + KOH(aq) → C₂H₅OH + KBr. Alcoholic KOH eliminates to ethene.
questions.trap: Ethene: alcoholic KOH.

questions.q: Chloroform is prepared in the laboratory by warming ethanol with
questions.x: Bleaching powder oxidises and chlorinates ethanol to chloral, then Ca(OH)₂ splits it to CHCl₃ (haloform reaction).

questions.q: Chloroform is stored in dark bottles filled to the brim because in air and light it forms
questions.x: 2CHCl₃ + O₂ → 2COCl₂ + 2HCl; ~1% ethanol is added to convert any phosgene to harmless diethyl carbonate.
questions.trap: Peroxides: that is for ethers.

questions.q: Chloroform reacts with concentrated nitric acid to give
questions.x: CHCl₃ + HNO₃ → CCl₃NO₂ + H₂O; chloropicrin is a tear gas and insecticide.

questions.q: Chloroform heated with silver powder gives
questions.x: 2CHCl₃ + 6Ag → HC≡CH + 6AgCl.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene is much less reactive than chloroethane towards nucleophiles because
o: Cl is more electronegative in chlorobenzene
the C–Cl bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance
questions.x: Cl lone pair delocalises into the ring; the sp² C–Cl bond is shorter and stronger and backside attack is blocked.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene is converted into phenol industrially (Dow's process) by
o: NaOH at about 623 K and 300 atm, then acidification
questions.x: Drastic conditions are needed because aryl C–Cl is strong: C₆H₅Cl + NaOH → C₆H₅ONa → C₆H₅OH.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride warmed with CuCl/HCl gives
questions.x: Sandmeyer reaction: C₆H₅N₂Cl → C₆H₅Cl + N₂.

questions.q: DDT is manufactured from chlorobenzene and
questions.x: Two chlorobenzene rings condense with chloral (CCl₃CHO), losing water.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene with sodium in dry ether gives
questions.x: Fittig reaction: 2C₆H₅Cl + 2Na → C₆H₅–C₆H₅ + 2NaCl. With CH₃Cl as well (Wurtz–Fittig) it gives toluene.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of alcohols
questions.q: With Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl₂), turbidity appears immediately with
questions.x: 3° alcohols react at once (stable 3° carbocation); 2° in ~5 min; 1° not at room temperature.

questions.q: In the oxo process, alcohols are made industrially from
o: an alkene, CO and H₂ (via an aldehyde)
questions.x: Hydroformylation (cobalt carbonyl catalyst): RCH=CH₂ + CO + H₂ → RCH₂CH₂CHO, which is hydrogenated to the alcohol.

questions.q: Hydroboration–oxidation of propene (B₂H₆, then H₂O₂/OH⁻) gives
questions.x: Boron adds to the terminal CH₂; overall anti-Markovnikov addition of water.
questions.trap: Propan-2-ol: acid-catalysed (Markovnikov) hydration.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – fermentation of sugar
questions.q: In alcoholic fermentation, glucose is converted to ethanol by the enzyme
questions.x: Invertase splits sucrose to glucose + fructose; zymase (yeast) converts glucose → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂.
questions.trap: Invertase: acts on sucrose, earlier step.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – types of ethanol
questions.q: Rectified spirit contains about
questions.x: 95.6% ethanol + water is an azeotrope, so distillation stops there; 100% is absolute alcohol.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – types of ethanol
questions.q: Power alcohol is
o: ethanol mixed with methanol to make it undrinkable
a mixture of petrol and absolute alcohol used as motor fuel
questions.x: Absolute alcohol blended with petrol (with a co-solvent such as benzene) is used as fuel.
questions.trap: Ethanol + methanol: methylated spirit.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – types of ethanol
questions.q: Methylated spirit is ethanol made unfit for drinking by adding
questions.x: Denatured alcohol: methanol is poisonous (causes blindness), so the spirit escapes excise duty.

questions.q: In Victor Meyer's test, a secondary alcohol gives
questions.x: 1° → red (nitrolic acid), 2° → blue (pseudonitrole), 3° → colourless.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of alcohols
questions.q: Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to give
questions.x: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂; shows weak acidity of alcohols.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of alcohols
questions.q: Propan-2-ol on oxidation with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ gives
questions.x: Secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones: (CH₃)₂CHOH → CH₃COCH₃.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of alcohols
questions.q: The best reagent to convert ethanol to chloroethane with only gaseous by-products is
questions.x: C₂H₅OH + SOCl₂ → C₂H₅Cl + SO₂↑ + HCl↑; product is easy to purify.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – preparation of phenol
questions.q: In the cumene process, phenol is obtained along with
questions.x: Cumene hydroperoxide is cleaved by dilute acid to phenol and propanone.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: Phenol with bromine water gives a white precipitate of
questions.x: –OH strongly activates the ring, so substitution at all o and p positions occurs without a catalyst.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: Neutral FeCl₃ solution with phenol gives
questions.x: Phenols form a violet iron(III) phenoxide complex: test for phenolic –OH.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: Sodium phenoxide heated with CO₂ under pressure (Kolbe's reaction), then acidified, gives
questions.x: CO₂ attacks the ortho position of phenoxide: o-hydroxybenzoic acid.
questions.trap: Salicylaldehyde: Reimer–Tiemann (CHCl₃/NaOH).

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because
o: the O–H bond in phenol is longer
the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance
questions.x: Negative charge of C₆H₅O⁻ delocalises into the ring; C₂H₅O⁻ is destabilised by +I of ethyl.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: Phenol with conc. HNO₃ (with conc. H₂SO₄) gives
questions.x: Picric acid = 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, a yellow explosive.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: Which is the most acidic?
questions.x: –NO₂ (−I, −R) stabilises the phenoxide; –CH₃ destabilises it; benzyl alcohol is an alcohol (weaker).

questions.q: Williamson's synthesis prepares ethers from
o: two alcohols and conc. H₂SO₄ only
a sodium alkoxide and an alkyl halide
questions.x: RONa + R′X → ROR′ + NaX (SN2).

questions.q: The best pair to prepare tert-butyl methyl ether is
o: tert-butyl alcohol + CH₃OH with conc. H₂SO₄
questions.x: SN2 needs an unhindered halide; tert-butyl bromide with a strong base gives isobutene by elimination.
questions.trap: tert-butyl bromide + CH₃ONa: elimination, not ether.

questions.s: Ethers – chemical properties of diethyl ether
questions.q: Diethyl ether heated with excess HI gives
questions.x: (C₂H₅)₂O + 2HI → 2C₂H₅I + H₂O. With limited cold HI: C₂H₅I + C₂H₅OH.
questions.trap: C₂H₅I + C₂H₅OH: that is with cold HI.

questions.s: Ethers – chemical properties of diethyl ether
questions.q: Old samples of diethyl ether can explode on distillation because they contain
o: peroxides formed by air and light
questions.x: Ethers slowly form hydroperoxides with O₂; removed by shaking with FeSO₄ solution.

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₃–O–CH₂CH₃ is
questions.x: Larger alkyl group is the parent; smaller alkoxy group is the prefix.
questions.trap: Ethoxymethane: larger group named as prefix.

questions.q: Anisole (methoxybenzene) heated with HI gives
questions.x: I⁻ attacks the methyl carbon; the aryl–O bond (partial double bond) is not broken.
questions.trap: Iodobenzene + methanol: aryl C–O does not break.

questions.q: Diethyl ether is a functional isomer of
questions.x: Both are C₄H₁₀O. Methoxypropane would be a metamer, not a functional isomer.

questions.s: Aldehydes and Ketones – preparation of carbonyl compounds
questions.q: Acetyl chloride with H₂ over Pd/BaSO₄ gives
questions.x: Rosenmund reduction: the poisoned catalyst stops at the aldehyde.

questions.s: Aldehydes and Ketones – preparation of carbonyl compounds
questions.q: An alkyl cyanide reduced with SnCl₂/HCl and then hydrolysed gives
questions.x: Stephen reduction: RCN → RCH=NH·HCl → RCHO.
questions.trap: Primary amine: LiAlH₄ or Na/C₂H₅OH reduction.

questions.s: Aldehydes and Ketones – preparation of carbonyl compounds
questions.q: Dry distillation of calcium acetate gives
questions.x: (CH₃COO)₂Ca → CH₃COCH₃ + CaCO₃.

questions.q: Which undergoes aldol condensation?
questions.x: Aldol needs an α-hydrogen; HCHO, C₆H₅CHO and (CH₃)₃CCHO have none (they give Cannizzaro).

questions.q: Tollens' reagent is
questions.x: [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ is reduced by aldehydes to a silver mirror.
questions.trap: Alkaline CuSO₄ + Rochelle salt: Fehling's solution.

questions.q: Which does not give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent?
questions.x: Ketones lack the oxidisable aldehydic H. HCOOH reduces Tollens' because of its –CHO-like H.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde does not reduce
questions.x: Aromatic aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent, KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇ (being oxidised to benzoic acid) but do not give red Cu₂O with Fehling's.

questions.q: Wolff–Kishner reduction converts a ketone to an alkane using
o: NH₂NH₂ and KOH in ethylene glycol on heating
questions.x: C=O → hydrazone → CH₂ with loss of N₂. Zn–Hg/HCl is Clemmensen (acidic).
questions.trap: Zn–Hg/HCl: Clemmensen.

questions.q: Acetaldehyde adds HCN to give
questions.x: Nucleophilic addition: CH₃CHO + HCN → CH₃CH(OH)CN.

questions.q: Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition is in the order
questions.x: Alkyl groups reduce the positive charge on C=O carbon (+I) and add steric hindrance.

questions.q: Toluene oxidised with chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂) and then hydrolysed gives
questions.x: Étard reaction stops at the aldehyde stage.
questions.trap: Benzoic acid: with KMnO₄.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde with alcoholic KCN gives
questions.x: Benzoin condensation: 2C₆H₅CHO → C₆H₅CH(OH)COC₆H₅ (CN⁻ catalyst).
questions.trap: Benzyl alcohol + benzoate: Cannizzaro with conc. NaOH.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde heated with acetic anhydride and sodium acetate gives
questions.x: Perkin reaction: C₆H₅CHO → C₆H₅CH=CHCOOH.

questions.q: Formaldehyde with ammonia forms
questions.x: 6HCHO + 4NH₃ → (CH₂)₆N₄ + 6H₂O; used as a urinary antiseptic.

questions.q: Number of carbonyl compounds (aldehydes + ketones) with formula C₄H₈O is
questions.x: Butanal, 2-methylpropanal (aldehydes) and butan-2-one (ketone).

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₃COCH₂CH₃ is
questions.x: 4-C chain with C=O at C-2 (lowest locant).

questions.q: The –CHO group in salicylaldehyde (from the Reimer–Tiemann reaction) is at which position relative to –OH?
questions.x: Dichlorocarbene attacks the ortho position of phenoxide mainly, giving o-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde).

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – relative reactivity
questions.q: Reactivity of acid derivatives towards nucleophilic acyl substitution is
questions.x: Better leaving group (Cl⁻ best, NH₂⁻ worst) and weaker resonance donation make the acyl carbon more reactive.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Acetic acid with Cl₂ in presence of red phosphorus gives
questions.x: Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction: α-H replaced by halogen.
questions.trap: Acetyl chloride: needs PCl₅ / SOCl₂.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – acid halide
questions.q: Acetic acid with PCl₅ gives
questions.x: CH₃COOH + PCl₅ → CH₃COCl + POCl₃ + HCl.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Formic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid because
o: the methyl group (+I) in acetic acid destabilises its anion
formic acid has more oxygen atoms
questions.x: pKa HCOOH 3.75, CH₃COOH 4.76 (lower pKa = stronger acid).

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Which carboxylic acid has the lowest pKa?
questions.x: No electron-releasing alkyl group, so HCOO⁻ is most stable; acidity falls as +I increases.
questions.trap: Propanoic acid: larger alkyl means weaker acid.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – natural acids
questions.q: The main acid in apples is
questions.x: Apple: malic; lemon: citric; grapes/tamarind: tartaric; sour milk: lactic.
questions.trap: Citric: lemons and oranges.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – amides
questions.q: Ammonium acetate on heating gives
questions.x: CH₃COONH₄ → CH₃CONH₂ + H₂O.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – amides
questions.q: Acetamide heated with P₂O₅ gives
questions.x: Dehydration: CH₃CONH₂ → CH₃CN + H₂O.
questions.trap: Methylamine: Hoffmann bromamide (Br₂/KOH).

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – esters
questions.q: Alkaline hydrolysis of an ester is called
questions.x: RCOOR′ + NaOH → RCOONa + R′OH; used to make soap from fats.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – acid anhydride
questions.q: Acetic anhydride is prepared by heating acetyl chloride with
questions.x: CH₃COCl + CH₃COONa → (CH₃CO)₂O + NaCl.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Acetic acid reduced with LiAlH₄ gives
questions.x: LiAlH₄ reduces –COOH all the way to the 1° alcohol –CH₂OH.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Pure acetic acid is called glacial acetic acid because it
o: freezes to ice-like crystals at about 16.6 °C
questions.x: Pure CH₃COOH solidifies just below room temperature in cold weather.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – esters
questions.q: Ethyl acetate treated with sodium ethoxide gives
questions.x: Claisen condensation: 2CH₃COOC₂H₅ → CH₃COCH₂COOC₂H₅ + C₂H₅OH.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Molar mass of acetic acid measured in benzene comes out nearly 120 because it
questions.x: Two –COOH groups pair by two H-bonds, so (CH₃COOH)₂ behaves as one particle (2 × 60 = 120).

questions.q: Nitrobenzene is prepared by heating benzene with
questions.x: Nitrating mixture generates NO₂⁺; temperature kept below about 60 °C to avoid dinitration.

questions.q: Oil of mirbane is
questions.x: Nitrobenzene is a pale yellow liquid smelling of bitter almonds, sold as oil of mirbane.
questions.trap: Benzaldehyde: oil of bitter almonds.

questions.q: Nitrobenzene reduced with Sn and conc. HCl gives
questions.x: Acidic reduction: C₆H₅NO₂ + 6[H] → C₆H₅NH₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.q: Nitrobenzene reduced with Zn dust and NH₄Cl (neutral medium) gives
questions.x: Neutral reduction stops at C₆H₅NHOH; acidic gives aniline; alkaline gives azo/hydrazo compounds.
questions.trap: Aniline: acidic (Sn/HCl) medium.

questions.q: Further nitration of nitrobenzene gives mainly
questions.x: –NO₂ deactivates the ring and directs meta.

questions.q: A nitroalkane reacts with HNO₂ and then gives a blue colour with NaOH. The nitroalkane is
questions.x: 2° → pseudonitrole (blue); 1° → nitrolic acid (red with NaOH); 3° has no α-H and does not react.

questions.q: CH₃–NO₂ and CH₃–O–N=O are
questions.x: Nitromethane (C–N bond) and methyl nitrite (C–O–N) have the same formula but different functional groups.

questions.q: Nitroethane reduced with Sn/HCl gives
questions.x: R–NO₂ + 6[H] → R–NH₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.q: The strongest base in aqueous solution is
questions.x: In water: 2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃ for methyl amines; 3° loses H-bond solvation of its cation and is crowded.
questions.trap: (CH₃)₃N: true in gas phase, not in water.

questions.q: In Hoffmann's method, a mixture of 1°, 2° and 3° amines is separated using
questions.x: 1° gives solid dialkyl oxamide, 2° gives liquid oxamic ester, 3° does not react.
questions.trap: Benzenesulphonyl chloride: Hinsberg's method.

questions.q: In Hoffmann's separation, the amine that does not react with diethyl oxalate is
questions.x: 3° amines have no N–H, so they cannot be acylated and are distilled off.

questions.q: Aniline with NaNO₂ and HCl at 0–5 °C gives
questions.x: Diazotisation: C₆H₅NH₂ + HNO₂ + HCl → C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + 2H₂O; low temperature keeps it stable.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride coupled with phenol in alkaline medium gives
questions.x: Electrophilic diazonium ion attacks para to –O⁻, forming an azo (–N=N–) dye.

questions.q: Aniline with bromine water gives a white precipitate of
questions.x: –NH₂ strongly activates o/p positions.

questions.q: Aniline is acetylated before nitration in order to
o: protect –NH₂ and reduce its ring activation
questions.x: Acetanilide is less activated and not oxidised by HNO₃; the –NHCOCH₃ group is later hydrolysed.

questions.q: Direct nitration of aniline gives a large amount of m-nitroaniline because
o: aniline is protonated to anilinium ion, which is meta-directing
questions.x: In strongly acidic nitrating mixture, C₆H₅NH₃⁺ (–I) forms and directs meta (about 47%).

questions.q: Ethanamine with nitrous acid gives
questions.x: Aliphatic diazonium salts decompose at once: C₂H₅NH₂ + HNO₂ → C₂H₅OH + N₂ + H₂O.

questions.q: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis gives
questions.x: Potassium phthalimide is alkylated once; hydrolysis releases pure RNH₂. Aryl halides do not react.

questions.q: Methyl cyanide reduced with Na and ethanol (Mendius reaction) gives
questions.x: CH₃C≡N + 4[H] → CH₃CH₂NH₂; carbon count stays 2.
questions.trap: Methylamine: losing a carbon (that is Hoffmann bromamide).

questions.q: Number of structurally isomeric amines of formula C₃H₉N is
questions.x: Propan-1-amine, propan-2-amine (1°), N-methylethanamine (2°), N,N-dimethylmethanamine (3°).

questions.q: (CH₃)₂CH–NH₂ is a
questions.x: Amine class depends on the number of alkyl groups on N (here one), not on the carbon type.
questions.trap: Secondary: confusing with secondary carbon.

questions.q: Decarboxylation of an α-amino acid (e.g. glycine, H₂NCH₂COOH) gives
o: a carboxylic acid with one less carbon
questions.x: Removal of CO₂: H₂NCH₂COOH → CH₃NH₂ + CO₂; in the body this gives amines like histamine from histidine.

questions.q: Grignard's reagent is prepared by reacting an alkyl halide with
questions.x: RX + Mg → RMgX; ether stabilises it and water must be absent.
questions.trap: Sodium in dry ether: Wurtz reaction.

questions.q: CH₃MgBr reacts with water to give
questions.x: Any compound with active H protonates the carbanion-like carbon: CH₃MgBr + H₂O → CH₄ + Mg(OH)Br.

questions.q: CH₃MgBr with formaldehyde, followed by hydrolysis, gives
questions.x: HCHO + RMgX → 1° alcohol RCH₂OH; here CH₃CH₂OH.

questions.q: CH₃MgBr with dry ice (CO₂), followed by hydrolysis, gives
questions.x: CH₃MgBr + CO₂ → CH₃COOMgBr → CH₃COOH.

questions.q: CH₃MgBr with acetone, followed by hydrolysis, gives
questions.x: Ketone + RMgX → 3° alcohol: (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₃.

questions.q: Ethyl acetate treated with excess CH₃MgBr and then hydrolysed gives
questions.x: First CH₃MgBr converts the ester to acetone; a second adds to give the 3° alcohol (CH₃)₃COH.
questions.trap: Acetone: it reacts further with excess reagent.

questions.q: CH₃MgBr reacts with CH₃CN, and the product is hydrolysed, to give
questions.x: RMgX adds to C≡N to form an imine salt, which hydrolyses to a ketone: CH₃COCH₃.

questions.q: Dimethylcadmium reacts with acetyl chloride to give
questions.x: (CH₃)₂Cd + 2CH₃COCl → 2CH₃COCH₃ + CdCl₂; R₂Cd is too weak to attack the ketone further.
questions.trap: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol: that would need excess Grignard.

questions.q: Lithium dimethylcuprate, a Gilman reagent, has the formula
questions.x: Gilman reagents R₂CuLi are made from 2RLi + CuI; used to couple with alkyl halides (Corey–House).

questions.q: In a Grignard reagent the C–Mg bond is polar with
questions.x: Mg (EN 1.2) is less electronegative than C (2.5), so carbon behaves as a carbanion (nucleophile).

questions.q: C₂H₅MgBr reacts with ethanol to give
questions.x: Ethanol's –OH proton converts C₂H₅MgBr to C₂H₆ + Mg(OC₂H₅)Br.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – Haber's process
questions.q: In Haber's process for ammonia, the catalyst is
questions.x: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, about 200 atm and 450–500 °C with finely divided Fe (Mo promoter).
questions.trap: V₂O₅: contact process.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – urea
questions.q: Urea is manufactured from
o: ammonia and carbon dioxide via ammonium carbamate
questions.x: 2NH₃ + CO₂ → NH₂COONH₄ → NH₂CONH₂ + H₂O.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – fertilizer
questions.q: Percentage of nitrogen in urea, NH₂CONH₂ (M = 60), is about
questions.trap: 23.3%: counting only one N atom.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – caustic soda
questions.q: In the diaphragm cell for caustic soda, the gas liberated at the cathode is
questions.x: Brine electrolysis: 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻ at cathode; Cl₂ at anode; the diaphragm keeps them apart.
questions.trap: Cl₂: anode product.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – cement
questions.q: Gypsum is added to cement clinker in order to
questions.x: 2–3% gypsum controls the rapid setting of calcium aluminates.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – paper and pulp
questions.q: In the kraft (sulphate) pulping process, wood chips are cooked with
questions.x: White liquor (NaOH + Na₂S) dissolves lignin, leaving cellulose fibres; Ca(HSO₃)₂ is the sulphite process.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – continuous and batch processing
questions.q: Continuous processing is preferred over batch processing when
o: many different small orders are made
one product is made in very large amounts
questions.x: Continuous plants (e.g. H₂SO₄, NH₃) run non-stop with lower cost per tonne; batch suits small, varied products like drugs.

questions.s: Applications of Non-metals, Metals and Compounds – baking soda
questions.q: Baking soda is
questions.x: On heating 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂, which makes dough rise; also an antacid.
questions.trap: Na₂CO₃·10H₂O: washing soda.

questions.s: Applications of Non-metals, Metals and Compounds – bleaching powder
questions.q: The chemical formula of bleaching powder is
questions.x: Made by passing Cl₂ over dry slaked lime; releases Cl₂ with acids.

questions.s: Applications of Non-metals, Metals and Compounds – hypo
questions.q: Hypo is used in photography because it
o: dissolves unexposed AgBr as a complex
questions.x: Na₂S₂O₃ + AgBr → Na₃[Ag(S₂O₃)₂] (soluble), fixing the image.

questions.s: Applications of Non-metals, Metals and Compounds – magnesia, epsom salt
questions.q: Epsom salt, used as a purgative, is
questions.x: Epsom salt = magnesium sulphate heptahydrate; MgO is magnesia (antacid).

questions.s: Applications of Non-metals, Metals and Compounds – formalin
questions.q: Formalin, used to preserve biological specimens, is
questions.x: Formalin = ~40% HCHO in water (with some methanol).

questions.s: Applications of Non-metals, Metals and Compounds – chloretone
questions.q: Chloretone, formed from chloroform and acetone, is used as
questions.x: Chloretone (1,1,1-trichloro-2-methylpropan-2-ol) is a sedative/hypnotic. Chloropicrin is the tear gas.
questions.trap: Tear gas: chloropicrin.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – polymer
questions.q: Teflon is a polymer of
questions.x: n CF₂=CF₂ → –(CF₂–CF₂)ₙ–; non-stick and chemically inert.
questions.trap: Vinyl chloride: PVC.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – dyes
questions.q: Indigo is classified as a
questions.x: Insoluble indigo is reduced in a vat to a soluble form, applied to cloth and re-oxidised in air.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – drugs
questions.q: Paracetamol is used mainly as
questions.x: It relieves pain and lowers fever (body temperature).
questions.trap: Antibiotic: kills bacteria; paracetamol does not.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – radioisotopes
questions.q: Radioisotope widely used in radiotherapy of cancer is
questions.x: Co-60 emits γ-rays used to destroy tumours; C-14 is for dating; I-131 for thyroid.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – buffer in daily life
questions.q: The pH of human blood (about 7.4) is maintained mainly by the buffer
questions.x: Carbonic acid–bicarbonate buffer neutralises added acid or base; phosphate and proteins help.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – applications of colloid
questions.q: Alum is added to muddy water to
o: coagulate the negatively charged colloidal clay particles
questions.x: Al³⁺ (high charge) neutralises negative sol particles, which settle (Hardy–Schulze rule).

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – osmotic pressure
questions.q: Sea water is made drinkable by
questions.x: Pressure greater than the osmotic pressure pushes water out through a semipermeable membrane, leaving salts.

questions.q: One mole of CoCl₃·5NH₃ is treated with excess AgNO₃ solution. Moles of AgCl precipitated are
questions.x: The complex is [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂: one Cl⁻ is bonded to Co (not ionisable), two are outside the bracket and precipitate as AgCl.
questions.trap: 3: counting the coordinated chloride too.

questions.q: Most metals do not liberate H₂ from nitric acid because
o: all metals become passive in nitric acid
HNO₃ is a strong oxidising agent, so NO₃⁻ is reduced instead of H⁺
questions.x: Any hydrogen formed is oxidised to water while HNO₃ is reduced to NO₂, NO, N₂O or NH₄⁺. Only Mg and Mn give H₂ with very dilute (1–2%) HNO₃.

questions.q: Which metal is extracted by electrolysis of its fused chloride rather than by reduction with carbon?
questions.x: Highly electropositive metals (Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al) form oxides more stable than CO, so carbon cannot reduce them; their fused salts are electrolysed.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – allotropes of carbon
questions.q: Which of the following is an amorphous (microcrystalline) form of carbon?
questions.x: Charcoal, coke, lamp black and carbon black are amorphous forms; diamond, graphite and fullerenes are crystalline allotropes.

questions.q: On distillation with conc. H₂SO₄, acetone forms an aromatic hydrocarbon. It is
questions.x: Three acetone molecules condense with loss of three H₂O (conc. H₂SO₄ dehydrates) to give 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene.

questions.q: Chlorine gas is evolved even without heating when concentrated HCl is added to
questions.x: 2KMnO₄ + 16HCl → 2KCl + 2MnCl₂ + 5Cl₂ + 8H₂O at room temperature; MnO₂ needs warming. CaCO₃ gives CO₂, Zn gives H₂.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – biomolecules (proteins)
questions.q: The –CO–NH– linkage that joins amino acids in a protein is called a
questions.x: The –COOH of one amino acid condenses with the –NH₂ of the next, losing water, to form an amide (peptide) bond.
questions.trap: Glycosidic bonds join sugar units.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – biomolecules (proteins)
questions.q: Complete hydrolysis of a protein (as in digestion) gives
questions.x: Hydrolysis breaks the peptide bonds. Carbohydrates give glucose, fats give fatty acids + glycerol, nucleic acids give nucleotides.

questions.q: Ammonia heated with excess methyl iodide finally gives
questions.x: Hofmann ammonolysis: NH₃ → 1° → 2° → 3° amine → quaternary salt (CH₃)₄N⁺I⁻ when the alkyl halide is in excess.
questions.trap: Methylamine forms only when ammonia is in excess.

questions.q: Iodine is obtained commercially from the ash of
questions.x: Marine algae concentrate iodide from sea water; the ash is treated with MnO₂ and H₂SO₄ to free I₂.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – oxides of sulphur and nitrogen (acid rain)
questions.q: Acid rain corrodes iron bridges and marble buildings mainly because it contains
o: H₂SO₄ and HNO₃ formed from SO₂ and NOₓ
questions.x: SO₂ and NOₓ from burning fuels form H₂SO₄ and HNO₃ in rain (pH < 5.6), which attack metals and CaCO₃.

questions.q: White phosphorus heated with concentrated H₂SO₄ is oxidised to
questions.x: P₄ + 10H₂SO₄ → 4H₃PO₄ + 10SO₂ + 4H₂O; hot conc. H₂SO₄ acts as an oxidising agent.
questions.trap: PH₃ forms with NaOH, not with H₂SO₄.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – alkaline earth metals
questions.q: Mg(OH)₂ is much less soluble in water than NaOH mainly because Mg(OH)₂ has
o: a much higher lattice energy (small, doubly charged Mg²⁺)
a lower hydration energy of Mg²⁺ than of Na⁺
questions.x: Mg²⁺ is small with charge 2+, so lattice energy is very high and outweighs its (also high) hydration energy.
questions.trap: Mg²⁺ actually has the higher hydration energy.

questions.q: Hydrogen peroxide is formed when cold dilute H₂SO₄ is added to
questions.x: Na₂O₂ is a true peroxide (O₂²⁻): Na₂O₂ + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + H₂O₂. Na₂O and ZnO give water; MnO₂ is a dioxide, not a peroxide.
questions.trap: MnO₂: a dioxide, not a peroxide.

questions.q: Hydrogen has oxidation number −1 in
questions.x: In ionic metal hydrides (NaH, CaH₂) hydrogen is H⁻ (−1); with non-metals it is +1.

questions.s: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes – nature of C–X bond
questions.q: Haloalkanes undergo nucleophilic substitution far more readily than alkanes because
o: the C–X bond is stronger than the C–H bond
the C–X bond is polar, leaving the carbon partially positive
questions.x: X is more electronegative than C, so Cδ+ attracts nucleophiles and X⁻ is a good leaving group; C–H is almost non-polar.

questions.q: Hydrolysis of ethyl isocyanide (C₂H₅NC) with dilute acid gives
questions.x: C₂H₅NC + 2H₂O → C₂H₅NH₂ + HCOOH (a primary amine). Nitriles (C₂H₅CN) instead give the acid + NH₃.
questions.trap: Propanoic acid + NH₃: that is ethyl cyanide (nitrile) hydrolysis.

questions.q: A nitrate warmed with zinc dust and NaOH solution gives
questions.x: Nascent hydrogen from Zn + NaOH reduces NO₃⁻ to NH₃ (test for nitrate, also with Devarda's alloy).

questions.q: The gas burnt with oxygen to give a flame of about 3000 °C for welding and cutting metals is
questions.x: Oxy-acetylene flame: C₂H₂ + O₂ gives a very hot flame because of the high heat of combustion and few product molecules.

questions.q: Dinitrogen (N₂) is chemically unreactive at room temperature mainly because
o: the N₂ molecule has unpaired electrons
the N≡N triple bond has a very high bond energy (946 kJ mol⁻¹)
questions.x: Breaking N≡N needs great energy, so N₂ reacts only at high temperature or with catalysts (Haber process).

questions.q: Ozone is prepared by passing dry oxygen through
questions.x: 3O₂ ⇌ 2O₃ is endothermic; a silent discharge (ozoniser) supplies energy without the heat that would decompose O₃.
questions.trap: Alkaline pyrogallol absorbs oxygen.

questions.q: The yellow street lamps used on highways contain the vapour of
questions.x: Excited Na atoms emit the golden-yellow D line (589 nm), the same colour as the sodium flame test.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – biomolecules (carbohydrates)
questions.q: The open-chain structure of glucose contains
o: one ketone C=O and five –OH groups
questions.x: Glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆, is an aldohexose: CHO–(CHOH)₄–CH₂OH. Fructose is the ketohexose.
questions.trap: Ketone C=O: that is fructose.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – esterification
questions.q: In the esterification of acetic acid with ethanol, a little concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as
o: an acid catalyst and dehydrating agent
questions.x: H⁺ protonates the C=O to speed the reaction, and conc. H₂SO₄ takes up water, shifting the equilibrium towards ethyl acetate.

questions.q: Benzene treated with acetyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ gives
questions.x: Friedel–Crafts acylation: AlCl₃ (Lewis acid) forms the acylium ion CH₃CO⁺, which substitutes the ring to give C₆H₅COCH₃.
questions.trap: Toluene: that is alkylation with CH₃Cl.

questions.s: Applications of Non-metals, Metals and Compounds – plaster of Paris
questions.q: Plaster of Paris heated above about 473 K gives 'dead burnt plaster', which is
o: anhydrous CaSO₄, which no longer sets with water
questions.x: Above ~473 K all water of crystallisation is lost; anhydrous CaSO₄ does not rehydrate quickly, so it cannot set.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – polymer
questions.q: Which polymer is made by addition polymerisation?
questions.x: Ethene molecules add to each other with no by-product. Nylon-6,6, terylene and bakelite are condensation polymers (water lost).

questions.q: Carbon is tetravalent in almost all organic compounds because in its excited state it has
questions.x: Ground state 2s² 2p² has only two unpaired electrons; promotion of one 2s electron gives 2s¹ 2p³ with four unpaired electrons, so carbon forms four bonds.
questions.trap: Two unpaired: that is the ground state, which would make carbon divalent.

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃ is
questions.x: Five-carbon chain with the C=O on carbon 3 from either end: pentan-3-one (common name diethyl ketone).

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₃CH(Cl)CH₂COOH is
questions.x: The –COOH carbon is C-1, so the chain is C1 (COOH), C2 (CH₂), C3 (CHCl), C4 (CH₃): 3-chlorobutanoic acid.
questions.trap: 2-chloro: numbering from the wrong end; COOH carbon is always C-1.

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₃–C≡C–CH(CH₃)₂ is
questions.x: Longest chain has 5 C; number from the end nearer the triple bond: triple bond at C-2, methyl at C-4.
questions.trap: 2-methylpent-3-yne: gives the triple bond a higher number.

questions.s: General Organic Chemistry – classification of organic compounds
questions.q: Which of the following is a heterocyclic compound?
questions.x: Pyridine (C₅H₅N) has a nitrogen atom in its ring. Benzene, cyclohexane and toluene have rings made of carbon only (homocyclic).

questions.q: Acetone (CH₃COCH₃) and prop-1-en-2-ol (CH₂=C(OH)CH₃) are
questions.x: They differ only in the position of a hydrogen atom and a double bond and exist in dynamic equilibrium: keto–enol tautomerism.

questions.q: Which compound does NOT show geometrical (cis–trans) isomerism?
questions.x: In (CH₃)₂C=CH₂ each double-bond carbon carries two identical groups, so cis and trans forms are impossible. The other three have two different groups on each carbon.

questions.s: General Organic Chemistry – heterolytic and homolytic bond fission
questions.q: Heterolytic fission of the C–Br bond in CH₃Br gives
questions.x: In heterolytic fission both bonding electrons go to the more electronegative atom (Br), forming ions.
questions.trap: CH₃· and Br·: that is homolytic fission (free radicals).

questions.q: The most stable free radical among the following is
questions.x: Radical stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl, because alkyl groups release electrons (+I and hyperconjugation) to the electron-deficient carbon.

questions.q: Which group shows a +R (electron-donating resonance) effect when attached to benzene?
questions.x: Oxygen of –OH has a lone pair it delocalises into the ring (+R). –NO₂, –CHO and –CN withdraw π electrons from the ring (−R).

questions.s: General Organic Chemistry – alkyl and aryl groups
questions.q: The group C₆H₅CH₂– is called
questions.x: Phenyl = C₆H₅–, benzyl = C₆H₅CH₂–, tolyl = CH₃C₆H₄–, benzoyl = C₆H₅CO–.
questions.trap: Phenyl: that is C₆H₅– without the CH₂.

questions.q: Which alkane cannot be prepared by the Wurtz reaction?
questions.x: Wurtz joins two alkyl groups (2RX + 2Na → R–R), so the product has at least two carbon atoms.

questions.q: Electrolysis of a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium propanoate (Kolbe's method) gives at the anode
questions.x: 2C₂H₅COO⁻ → 2C₂H₅· + 2CO₂ at the anode; two ethyl radicals join: C₂H₅–C₂H₅ = butane.
questions.trap: Propane: students keep all three carbons of the acid; CO₂ is lost.

questions.q: 1,2-Dibromoethane heated with excess alcoholic KOH (or NaNH₂) gives
questions.x: Two successive dehydrohalogenations remove 2 HBr: BrCH₂CH₂Br → CH₂=CHBr → HC≡CH.
questions.trap: Ethene: formed when the dibromide is heated with zinc dust.

questions.q: Ozonolysis of but-1-ene (CH₂=CH–CH₂CH₃) followed by Zn/H₂O gives
questions.x: The C=C is cut and each carbon becomes C=O: CH₂= gives HCHO, =CHCH₂CH₃ gives CH₃CH₂CHO.
questions.trap: Two ethanal: that is from but-2-ene.

questions.q: An alkene C₆H₁₂ gives only propanone on ozonolysis. The alkene is
questions.x: (CH₃)₂C=C(CH₃)₂ splits into two (CH₃)₂C=O. Hex-3-ene gives propanal; 2-methylpent-2-ene gives propanone + propanal.

questions.q: Ethene reacts with hypochlorous acid (Cl₂ water) to give
questions.x: HOCl adds as Cl⁺ and OH⁻ across the double bond: CH₂=CH₂ + HOCl → ClCH₂CH₂OH.

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT react with sodamide (NaNH₂) to form a sodium salt?
questions.x: Only terminal alkynes have the acidic ≡C–H. But-2-yne (CH₃C≡CCH₃) has no H on the triple-bonded carbons.

questions.q: A petrol with octane number 80 knocks like a mixture of
questions.x: Octane scale: iso-octane = 100, n-heptane = 0; the octane number is the % of iso-octane in the matching mixture.
questions.trap: Cetane mixture: that is the scale for diesel.

questions.q: Number of π electrons in naphthalene (C₁₀H₈) is
questions.x: Five C=C bonds × 2 = 10 π electrons = 4n + 2 with n = 2, so naphthalene is aromatic.

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene (toluene)
questions.q: Chlorine passed into boiling toluene in sunlight (no catalyst) gives mainly
questions.x: Light and heat give Cl· radicals that substitute the side-chain CH₃: C₆H₅CH₃ → C₆H₅CH₂Cl. With FeCl₃ in the dark, the ring is chlorinated (o/p).
questions.trap: o/p-Chlorotoluene: needs a Lewis acid catalyst in the dark.
