questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: Which group activates the benzene ring and directs an incoming electrophile to ortho and para positions?
questions.x: –OH donates electron density by resonance, increasing it most at o and p positions. The other three are deactivating and meta-directing.

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene (toluene)
questions.q: Toluene on oxidation with alkaline KMnO₄ followed by acidification gives
questions.x: Strong oxidants convert the whole side chain to –COOH, leaving the ring intact: C₆H₅CH₃ → C₆H₅COOH.
questions.trap: Benzaldehyde: needs a mild reagent such as CrO₂Cl₂ (Etard).

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: Benzene with hydrogen over nickel at about 473 K gives
questions.x: C₆H₆ + 3H₂ → C₆H₁₂; under forcing conditions benzene adds three molecules of H₂.

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: Correct order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitution is
questions.x: Electron-donating groups activate the ring (–OH strongly by +R, –CH₃ weakly by +I); –NO₂ withdraws electrons and deactivates it.

questions.q: In the Friedel–Crafts reaction, anhydrous AlCl₃ acts as
o: a Lewis acid that generates the electrophile
questions.x: AlCl₃ accepts Cl⁻ from RCl or RCOCl, forming R⁺ or RCO⁺ (and AlCl₄⁻), which attacks the ring.

questions.q: Benzene does not decolourise bromine water at room temperature (unlike ethene) because
o: addition would destroy its stable delocalised π system
bromine water does not contain Br₂
questions.x: Resonance stabilisation makes benzene prefer substitution (with a catalyst) that keeps the aromatic ring, rather than addition across a C=C.

questions.q: Benzenesulphonic acid heated with superheated steam (dilute acid) gives
questions.x: Sulphonation is reversible: C₆H₅SO₃H + H₂O → C₆H₆ + H₂SO₄ (desulphonation).
questions.trap: Phenol: needs fusion of the sodium salt with NaOH.

questions.s: Aromatic Hydrocarbons – chemical properties of benzene
questions.q: The electrophile in chlorination of benzene with Cl₂ and anhydrous FeCl₃ is
questions.x: FeCl₃ + Cl₂ → FeCl₄⁻ + Cl⁺; the chloronium ion attacks the ring to give chlorobenzene.
questions.trap: Cl·: radicals form only in light, giving addition to benzene.

questions.s: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes – preparation of monohaloalkanes
questions.q: Bromoethane warmed with NaI in dry acetone gives iodoethane. This is called the
questions.x: Halogen exchange: NaBr formed is insoluble in acetone and precipitates, driving the reaction forward.
questions.trap: Swarts: exchange giving fluorides with AgF/Hg₂F₂.

questions.s: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes – preparation of monohaloalkanes
questions.q: CH₃Br heated with AgF gives CH₃F. The reaction is the
questions.x: Alkyl fluorides are made from alkyl chlorides/bromides with metallic fluorides such as AgF, Hg₂F₂ or SbF₃.

questions.s: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes – preparation of monohaloalkanes
questions.q: Silver acetate refluxed with Br₂ in CCl₄ (Hunsdiecker reaction) gives
questions.x: CH₃COOAg + Br₂ → CH₃Br + CO₂ + AgBr: the product has one carbon fewer than the acid.
questions.trap: Bromoethane: forgetting CO₂ is lost.

questions.q: Number of structurally isomeric monochloro compounds of formula C₄H₉Cl is
questions.x: 1-Chlorobutane, 2-chlorobutane, 1-chloro-2-methylpropane and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene and methyl chloride heated with sodium in dry ether give
questions.x: Wurtz–Fittig reaction: C₆H₅Cl + CH₃Cl + 2Na → C₆H₅CH₃ + 2NaCl.
questions.trap: Biphenyl: Fittig reaction, chlorobenzene alone with Na.

questions.q: Chloroform warmed with aniline and alcoholic KOH gives an offensive-smelling
questions.x: Carbylamine reaction: C₆H₅NH₂ + CHCl₃ + 3KOH → C₆H₅NC + 3KCl + 3H₂O; a test for primary amines and for chloroform.
questions.trap: Phenyl cyanide (benzonitrile): C–N bonded the other way.

questions.s: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes – properties of monohaloalkanes
questions.q: Bromoethane treated with alcoholic KCN and the product then hydrolysed with dilute acid gives
questions.x: C₂H₅Br + KCN → C₂H₅CN (one extra carbon); hydrolysis: C₂H₅CN + 2H₂O → C₂H₅COOH + NH₃ (NH₄⁺ in acid).
questions.trap: Acetic acid: missing the carbon added by CN.

questions.q: Chloroform boiled with aqueous NaOH gives
questions.x: CHCl₃ + 4NaOH → HCOONa + 3NaCl + 2H₂O; the gem-triol HC(OH)₃ loses water to formic acid, which forms its sodium salt.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – preparation of monohydric alcohols
questions.q: Propene with water in the presence of dilute H₂SO₄ gives mainly
questions.x: Acid-catalysed hydration follows Markovnikov's rule: H⁺ adds to CH₂, giving the 2° carbocation, then OH on C-2.
questions.trap: Propan-1-ol: from hydroboration–oxidation (anti-Markovnikov).

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: Phenol heated with CCl₄ and aqueous NaOH, then acidified, gives
questions.x: Reimer–Tiemann reaction with CCl₄ puts –COOH ortho to –OH; with CHCl₃ it gives salicylaldehyde (–CHO).
questions.trap: Salicylaldehyde: that needs CHCl₃.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of alcohols
questions.q: Vapour of 2-methylpropan-2-ol passed over heated copper at 573 K gives
questions.x: A 3° alcohol has no H on the carbinol carbon, so it cannot be dehydrogenated; it is dehydrated to the alkene. 1° gives an aldehyde, 2° a ketone.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – types of alcohol (methanol)
questions.q: Drinking methanol (wood spirit) even in small amounts can cause
questions.x: Methanol is oxidised in the body to formaldehyde and formic acid, which damage the optic nerve.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: Phenol does not liberate CO₂ from sodium bicarbonate solution because
o: phenol is a weaker acid than carbonic acid
phenol is not acidic at all
questions.x: pKa of phenol ≈ 10 versus 6.4 for H₂CO₃; carboxylic acids (pKa 4–5) are stronger and do liberate CO₂, which distinguishes them from phenol.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – properties of phenol
questions.q: The least acidic of the following is
questions.x: Electron-donating –CH₃ destabilises the phenoxide ion (pKa ≈ 10.3); –Cl and –NO₂ withdraw electrons and increase acidity.

questions.s: Alcohols and Phenols – types of ethanol
questions.q: Rectified spirit cannot be turned into absolute alcohol by simple fractional distillation because
o: ethanol and water have the same boiling point
95.6% ethanol forms a constant-boiling azeotrope with water
water is less volatile than ethanol
questions.x: The azeotrope boils at about 78.1 °C without change in composition; the last water is removed with quicklime or by azeotropic distillation with benzene.

questions.q: Total number of structural isomers of formula C₃H₈O (alcohols and ethers) is
questions.x: Propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol and methoxyethane.

questions.q: Ethanol in excess heated with conc. H₂SO₄ at about 413 K (140 °C) gives
questions.x: At 413 K with excess alcohol: 2C₂H₅OH → C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + H₂O. At 443 K with excess acid, ethene forms.
questions.trap: Ethene: higher temperature (443 K) and excess acid.

questions.s: Ethers – chemical properties of diethyl ether
questions.q: Diethyl ether dissolves in cold concentrated H₂SO₄ because it
o: accepts a proton to form an oxonium salt
questions.x: The O lone pairs make ether a Lewis base: (C₂H₅)₂O + H₂SO₄ → [(C₂H₅)₂OH]⁺ HSO₄⁻, which dissolves; alkanes do not.

questions.s: Ethers – chemical properties of diethyl ether
questions.q: Diethyl ether heated with PCl₅ gives
questions.x: (C₂H₅)₂O + PCl₅ → 2C₂H₅Cl + POCl₃; ether has no –OH, so no HCl is evolved (unlike alcohols).

questions.q: tert-Butyl methyl ether heated with one mole of HI gives
questions.x: The protonated ether cleaves by SN1, forming the stable 3° carbocation: (CH₃)₃C⁺ + I⁻ → (CH₃)₃CI; CH₃OH is released.
questions.trap: Methyl iodide + tert-butanol: SN2 logic, valid only when both groups are 1°/methyl.

questions.q: Anisole (C₆H₅OCH₃) reacts with bromine in ethanoic acid to give mainly
questions.x: –OCH₃ activates the ring by +R and is ortho/para-directing; the para isomer dominates (less crowded).

questions.q: CH₃–O–C₂H₅ is classified as
questions.x: The two alkyl groups on oxygen are different (methyl and ethyl). In a simple ether, e.g. C₂H₅OC₂H₅, they are the same.

questions.q: Number of isomeric ethers of formula C₄H₁₀O is
questions.x: C₂H₅OC₂H₅, CH₃OCH₂CH₂CH₃ and CH₃OCH(CH₃)₂ (metamers of one another).
questions.trap: 7: counting the four alcohols too.

questions.q: Benzene treated with CO and HCl in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ (and CuCl) gives
questions.x: Gattermann–Koch reaction: CO + HCl act like 'HCOCl', formylating the ring to C₆H₅CHO.

questions.q: Ethanal with dilute NaOH at room temperature gives
questions.x: Aldol addition: the carbanion from one CH₃CHO adds to the C=O of another: CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO. Heating dehydrates it to but-2-enal.
questions.trap: Ethanol + acetate: Cannizzaro, only for aldehydes without α-H.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde and formaldehyde heated with concentrated NaOH give
questions.x: Crossed Cannizzaro: HCHO is the more easily oxidised aldehyde, so it becomes formate while benzaldehyde is reduced to C₆H₅CH₂OH.
questions.trap: Sodium benzoate + methanol: the roles reversed.

questions.q: 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine (Brady's reagent) gives a yellow-orange precipitate with
questions.x: Any C=O of an aldehyde or ketone condenses with it to form a 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone.

questions.q: Acetaldehyde warmed with Fehling's solution gives a red precipitate of
questions.x: The aldehyde reduces Cu²⁺ (blue) to copper(I) oxide (red) and is oxidised to acetate.
questions.trap: Ag: silver mirror is Tollens' test.

questions.q: Which does NOT give the iodoform test?
questions.x: Iodoform needs CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)–. Pentan-3-one (C₂H₅COC₂H₅) has neither.

questions.q: Acetaldehyde reacts with hydroxylamine (NH₂OH) to give
questions.x: CH₃CHO + NH₂OH → CH₃CH=NOH + H₂O (addition–elimination).
questions.trap: Hydrazone: formed with hydrazine, NH₂NH₂.

questions.q: Butanal and butanone are
questions.x: Both are C₄H₈O but contain different functional groups (–CHO and >C=O).

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Which chloro-substituted acid is the strongest?
questions.x: Each Cl (−I) stabilises the carboxylate ion more; three Cl atoms make trichloroacetic acid (pKa ≈ 0.7) the strongest.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Formic acid reduces Tollens' reagent, but acetic acid does not, because formic acid
questions.x: HCOOH (H–CO–OH) is oxidised to CO₂ + H₂O, reducing Ag⁺ to a silver mirror.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – esters
questions.q: Ethyl acetate treated with ammonia gives
questions.x: Ammonolysis: CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NH₃ → CH₃CONH₂ + C₂H₅OH; NH₃ replaces the –OC₂H₅ group.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – acid halide
questions.q: Acetyl chloride fumes in moist air because it
questions.x: CH₃COCl + H₂O → CH₃COOH + HCl; HCl forms droplets of hydrochloric acid with moisture.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – acid anhydride
questions.q: Aniline reacts with acetic anhydride to give
questions.x: Acetylation: C₆H₅NH₂ + (CH₃CO)₂O → C₆H₅NHCOCH₃ + CH₃COOH.
questions.trap: Benzanilide: needs benzoyl chloride.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – isomerism
questions.q: Number of carboxylic acids of formula C₄H₈O₂ is
questions.x: Butanoic acid and 2-methylpropanoic acid. (Esters of the same formula are functional isomers, not acids.)
questions.trap: 4: counting the esters as well.

questions.s: Carboxylic Acid and its Derivatives – chemical properties
questions.q: Which is the strongest acid?
questions.x: pKa: benzoic acid 4.2, acetic acid 4.76, phenol 10, ethanol about 16. The sp² phenyl group withdraws electrons from –COOH.

questions.q: Bromoethane heated with alcoholic AgNO₂ gives mainly
questions.x: AgNO₂ is covalent, so the nitrite ion attacks through N, giving C₂H₅–NO₂. Ionic KNO₂/NaNO₂ attacks through O, giving ethyl nitrite.
questions.trap: Ethyl nitrite: the main product with KNO₂.

questions.q: Which nitroalkane does NOT dissolve in aqueous NaOH?
questions.x: Nitroalkanes with α-hydrogen are acidic (strong −I of –NO₂) and dissolve in NaOH as salts. (CH₃)₃C–NO₂ has no α-H.

questions.q: A primary nitroalkane with nitrous acid and then NaOH gives
questions.x: Victor Meyer's test for nitroalkanes: 1° → nitrolic acid (red in alkali), 2° → pseudonitrole (blue), 3° → no reaction.
questions.trap: Blue: that is the secondary nitroalkane.

questions.q: Nitrobenzene reduced with LiAlH₄ gives
questions.x: LiAlH₄ reduces aromatic nitro compounds to azo compounds, C₆H₅–N=N–C₆H₅. Sn/HCl gives aniline; Zn/NH₄Cl gives N-phenylhydroxylamine.
questions.trap: Aniline: that is Sn/HCl or H₂/Ni.

questions.q: Nitroethane boiled with concentrated HCl gives
questions.x: Primary nitroalkanes are hydrolysed by hot conc. HCl: CH₃CH₂NO₂ + H₂O → CH₃COOH + NH₂OH (as NH₂OH·HCl).

questions.q: IUPAC name of CH₃CH(NO₂)CH₃ is
questions.x: Three-carbon chain with –NO₂ on C-2; it is a secondary nitroalkane.

questions.q: Nitrobenzene with Cl₂ in the presence of FeCl₃ gives mainly
questions.x: –NO₂ withdraws electrons (−I, −R) and deactivates the o/p positions most, so substitution occurs at meta.

questions.q: In Hinsberg's test, the amine whose product with benzenesulphonyl chloride dissolves in aqueous KOH is
questions.x: 1° amine gives RNHSO₂C₆H₅, whose N–H is acidic, so it dissolves in alkali. 2° gives an insoluble sulphonamide (no N–H); 3° does not react.

questions.q: A secondary amine with nitrous acid gives
o: an alcohol with evolution of N₂
questions.x: R₂NH + HONO → R₂N–N=O + H₂O (Liebermann nitroso reaction). Aliphatic 1° amines give alcohol + N₂; aniline at 0–5 °C gives a diazonium salt.
questions.trap: Alcohol + N₂: that is a primary aliphatic amine.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride treated with hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂) gives
questions.x: H₃PO₂ reduces –N₂⁺ to –H: C₆H₅N₂Cl + H₃PO₂ + H₂O → C₆H₆ + N₂ + H₃PO₃ + HCl.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride warmed with aqueous KI gives
questions.x: C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + KI → C₆H₅I + N₂ + KCl; no copper catalyst is needed.

questions.q: An aqueous solution of benzenediazonium chloride on warming gives
questions.x: C₆H₅N₂Cl + H₂O → C₆H₅OH + N₂ + HCl; this is why diazotisation is done at 0–5 °C.

questions.q: Aniline heated with conc. H₂SO₄ at about 453–473 K gives
questions.x: Anilinium hydrogen sulphate rearranges on heating to p-aminobenzenesulphonic acid (sulphanilic acid), used to make sulpha drugs.

questions.q: Number of isomeric amines of formula C₂H₇N is
questions.x: Ethanamine (CH₃CH₂NH₂, 1°) and N-methylmethanamine ((CH₃)₂NH, 2°).

questions.q: Acetamide reduced with LiAlH₄ gives
questions.x: Reduction keeps all carbons: CH₃CONH₂ + 4[H] → CH₃CH₂NH₂ + H₂O.
questions.trap: Methanamine: from Hofmann's Br₂/KOH reaction, which removes one carbon.

questions.q: CH₃MgBr with acetaldehyde, followed by hydrolysis, gives
questions.x: CH₃⁻ adds to the C=O of CH₃CHO; hydrolysis gives (CH₃)₂CHOH, a 2° alcohol (any aldehyde other than HCHO gives a 2° alcohol).

questions.q: Grignard reagents are prepared in absolutely dry ether because they
o: react with water to form alkanes
questions.x: Water's acidic H protonates the carbanion-like carbon: RMgX + H₂O → RH + Mg(OH)X. Dry ether also stabilises RMgX by coordinating to Mg.

questions.q: CH₃MgBr reacts with ethyne. The gas evolved is
questions.x: Terminal alkyne H is acidic: CH₃MgBr + HC≡CH → CH₄ + HC≡CMgBr (any compound with active H gives the alkane).

questions.q: Which of the following is an organolithium compound?
questions.x: Organolithium compounds (RLi) contain a direct C–Li bond. LiAlH₄, CH₃COOLi and CH₃OLi have no carbon–lithium bond.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an organometallic compound?
questions.x: An organometallic compound must have a direct metal–carbon bond; in C₂H₅ONa sodium is bonded to oxygen.

questions.q: Lithium dimethylcuprate, (CH₃)₂CuLi, reacts with bromoethane to give
questions.x: Corey–House synthesis: R₂CuLi + R′X → R–R′. Here CH₃ + C₂H₅ = CH₃CH₂CH₃.
questions.trap: Butane: coupling two ethyl groups (Wurtz).

questions.q: Which alcohol CANNOT be prepared by adding a Grignard reagent to a carbonyl compound?
questions.x: The Grignard alkyl group adds a carbon to the carbonyl carbon, so the smallest product is ethanol (CH₃MgX + HCHO).

questions.q: In Langmuir's atomic hydrogen torch, the very high temperature comes from
o: hydrogen atoms recombining to H₂ on the metal surface
questions.x: H₂ is split into atoms in an electric arc (absorbing 436 kJ/mol); on the metal the atoms recombine, releasing this energy as intense heat for welding.

questions.q: Heavy water can be obtained by
questions.x: H₂ is liberated faster than D₂ during electrolysis, so the remaining water becomes richer in D₂O.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – types of oxides
questions.q: Among the oxides of manganese, the most acidic is
questions.x: Acidic character rises with oxidation state: MnO (+2) basic, MnO₂ (+4) amphoteric, Mn₂O₇ (+7) acidic (gives HMnO₄).

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – types of oxides
questions.q: Red lead, Pb₃O₄, is classified as a
questions.x: Pb₃O₄ behaves as a combination of PbO and PbO₂; with HNO₃ it gives Pb(NO₃)₂ and PbO₂. It contains no O–O bond.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – test of ozone
questions.q: Ozone turns moist starch-iodide paper blue because it
questions.x: O₃ + 2KI + H₂O → 2KOH + I₂ + O₂; I₂ gives a blue-black colour with starch.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – chemical properties of ozone
questions.q: Ozone is used to restore old oil paintings blackened by PbS because it
o: oxidises black PbS to white PbSO₄
questions.x: PbS + 4O₃ → PbSO₄ + 4O₂; white lead sulphate restores the original colour.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – chemical properties of ammonia
questions.q: Ammonia passed over heated copper(II) oxide gives
questions.x: 3CuO + 2NH₃ → 3Cu + N₂ + 3H₂O: ammonia acts as a reducing agent.

questions.q: Compared with ammonia, phosphine (PH₃) is
questions.x: P is larger and less electronegative; its lone pair is in a diffuse orbital, less available for H⁺. PH₄⁺ salts form only with strong acids like HI.

questions.q: Chlorine water added to KBr solution gives an orange-brown colour because
questions.x: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂; a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from its salt.

questions.q: The only non-metal that is a liquid at room temperature is
questions.x: Br₂ is a red-brown volatile liquid (bp 59 °C). Mercury is the only liquid metal.
questions.trap: Mercury: a liquid, but a metal.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – HCl, HBr and HI
questions.q: HBr is prepared by heating KBr with conc. H₃PO₄ rather than conc. H₂SO₄ because
o: H₂SO₄ oxidises some HBr to Br₂
H₂SO₄ does not react with KBr
questions.x: 2HBr + H₂SO₄ → Br₂ + SO₂ + 2H₂O. H₃PO₄ is non-volatile and non-oxidising, so pure HBr is obtained.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – chemical properties of carbon monoxide
questions.q: CO combines with Cl₂ in sunlight to give
questions.x: CO + Cl₂ → COCl₂ (carbonyl chloride), a poisonous gas.
questions.trap: Chloropicrin: CCl₃NO₂, from chloroform + HNO₃.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – chemical properties of hydrogen sulphide
questions.q: H₂S and SO₂ react in the presence of moisture to deposit
questions.x: 2H₂S + SO₂ → 3S + 2H₂O: H₂S is oxidised and SO₂ acts as an oxidising agent.

questions.s: Chemistry of Non-metals – allotropes of carbon
questions.q: Graphite is used as a lubricant because
o: its layers are held by weak forces and slide over each other
questions.x: Within a layer C atoms are strongly bonded (sp²); layers are 340 pm apart, held by weak van der Waals forces.

questions.q: Copper is recovered from low-grade ores by leaching with dilute H₂SO₄ and then adding scrap iron. This is
questions.x: The metal is dissolved as Cu²⁺ and then displaced by a more reactive metal: Fe + Cu²⁺ → Fe²⁺ + Cu.

questions.q: In the extraction of copper, the 'matte' obtained from the smelting furnace is mainly
questions.x: Roasted ore is smelted with silica: FeO forms FeSiO₃ slag and the molten sulphides (Cu₂S + some FeS) form the matte.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – alkali and alkaline earth metals
questions.q: Lithium shows a diagonal relationship with
questions.x: Li⁺ and Mg²⁺ have similar charge/size ratios; both form nitrides, normal oxides and decomposable carbonates.
questions.trap: Aluminium: diagonal partner of beryllium.

questions.q: Sodium burnt in excess air (oxygen) gives mainly
questions.x: 2Na + O₂ → Na₂O₂. Li gives Li₂O, while K, Rb and Cs form superoxides MO₂.

questions.q: An aqueous solution of sodium carbonate is alkaline because
o: CO₃²⁻ is hydrolysed, producing OH⁻ ions
questions.x: Salt of a strong base and weak acid: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – alkaline earth metals
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal oxide is amphoteric?
questions.x: BeO dissolves in acids and in alkalis (forming beryllates); the other alkaline earth oxides are basic.

questions.q: Spin-only magnetic moment of Cr³⁺ (Z of Cr = 24) is about
questions.x: Cr³⁺ is 3d³ with n = 3 unpaired electrons: μ = √(n(n+2)) = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – shape of complex ions
questions.q: Shape of Ni(CO)₄ is
questions.x: Ni(0) uses sp³ hybrid orbitals for four CO ligands, so Ni(CO)₄ is tetrahedral and diamagnetic.
questions.trap: Square planar: that is [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ (dsp²).

questions.q: Zinc oxide is white when cold. On heating it turns
o: yellow, and becomes white again on cooling
questions.x: On heating ZnO loses a little oxygen, creating lattice defects that absorb light; the change reverses on cooling.

questions.q: Mercury is extracted from cinnabar by
o: roasting the sulphide in air, which gives mercury directly
questions.x: HgS + O₂ → Hg + SO₂; HgO is unstable at this temperature, so mercury vapour distils off and is condensed.

questions.s: Chemistry of Metals – steel (open hearth process)
questions.q: The open hearth (Siemens–Martin) process for making steel uses
o: regenerative heating of air and fuel gas by hot exhaust gases
pure oxygen blown onto molten pig iron
questions.x: Waste gases heat chequered brick chambers that then preheat the incoming air and producer gas, giving a very high hearth temperature.
questions.trap: Pure oxygen: that is the basic oxygen (L–D) process.

questions.q: The purest commercial form of iron (least carbon) is
questions.x: Wrought iron has only about 0.1–0.25% carbon; steel has more, and cast iron and pig iron about 2.5–4.5%.

questions.q: The main cation inside body cells is
questions.x: K⁺ is the chief intracellular cation; Na⁺ is the chief extracellular cation (maintained by the Na⁺/K⁺ pump).
questions.trap: Na⁺: mainly outside the cell.

questions.q: In the body, Mg²⁺ ions are especially needed for
o: enzymes that use ATP (as the Mg–ATP complex)
questions.x: Most ATP-using enzymes (kinases) act on Mg–ATP; Mg²⁺ is also needed for nerve and muscle function.

questions.q: Copper is biologically important as a constituent of
questions.x: Cu is in cytochrome c oxidase (respiration) and ceruloplasmin. Co is in B₁₂, Mg in chlorophyll, Fe in haemoglobin.

questions.q: Chronic lead poisoning causes anaemia mainly because lead
o: replaces Fe in haemoglobin to carry more O₂
questions.x: Pb²⁺ binds –SH groups of enzymes such as δ-aminolaevulinic acid dehydratase, blocking haem formation.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – ammonia (Haber's process)
questions.q: High pressure is used in Haber's process because
o: ammonia is a liquid at high pressure
the forward reaction decreases the number of gas molecules
the catalyst works only at high pressure
questions.x: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: 4 mol gas → 2 mol gas, so by Le Chatelier's principle high pressure shifts equilibrium to NH₃.
questions.trap: Endothermic: the reaction is exothermic.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – sulphuric acid (Contact process)
questions.q: In the contact process, SO₃ is absorbed in 98% H₂SO₄ rather than in water because
o: with water it forms a dense mist of acid that is hard to condense
questions.x: SO₃ + H₂SO₄ → H₂S₂O₇ (oleum), which is then diluted with water to the required strength.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – sodium carbonate (Solvay process)
questions.q: The main by-product of the Solvay process is
questions.x: NH₃ is recovered from NH₄Cl with slaked lime: 2NH₄Cl + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + 2NH₃ + 2H₂O, leaving CaCl₂ as waste.
questions.trap: NH₄Cl: recycled to recover ammonia.

questions.s: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry and Manufacturing Processes – environmental effect of chemical industry
questions.q: Dust particles in chimney gases of factories are removed by
questions.x: Charged particles move to the oppositely charged electrodes and are collected, so cleaner gas leaves the chimney.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – fertilizer
questions.q: Superphosphate of lime is
questions.x: Rock phosphate + conc. H₂SO₄: Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → Ca(H₂PO₄)₂ + 2CaSO₄; the dihydrogen phosphate is water-soluble.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – polymer
questions.q: Bakelite is a condensation polymer of
questions.x: Phenol–formaldehyde resin; it is a thermosetting plastic used for switches and handles.
questions.trap: Urea + formaldehyde: urea-formaldehyde resin.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – polymer
questions.q: Vulcanisation of natural rubber is done by heating it with
questions.x: Sulphur forms cross-links between cis-polyisoprene chains, making the rubber harder, stronger and less sticky.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – radioisotopes
questions.q: The radioisotope used to diagnose and treat thyroid disorders is
questions.x: The thyroid takes up iodine; I-131 (β and γ emitter) is used for imaging and destroying overactive thyroid tissue.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – applications of colloid
questions.q: Alum or FeCl₃ stops bleeding from a small cut because it
questions.x: Blood is a negatively charged colloid; highly charged Al³⁺/Fe³⁺ ions neutralise it and cause clotting.

questions.s: Chemistry in Service to Mankind – drugs
questions.q: Dettol, a common antiseptic, is a mixture of
questions.x: Chloroxylenol with terpineol is mild enough for skin and wounds; tincture of iodine is iodine in alcohol.
